data.title: Lock granularity — Mutex held for entire solve_dirty
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-9235dd20`

**tags:** `performance`, `architectural`

**pi id:** `TODO-9235dd20`

**tags:** `performance`, `architectural`

---

## Problem

The `parking_lot::Mutex<UniswapEngine>` is held for the entire `solve_dirty` call including all `resolve_path` + `solve_path` work. For 100-200 affected paths, that's ~5-20ms of lock hold time where Python is blocked out. This matters because Python reads `latest_results()` under the same lock.

Location: `rust/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine.rs` (engine) + `rust/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine_pump.rs` (pump lock sites)

## Fix Options

1. **Compute results under the lock, then release before sending via channel** — the channel send is non-blocking (unbounded), so there's no reason to hold the lock during `compute_diff_and_send`.

2. **Split into read-lock (for pool state) and write-lock (for results)** — `resolve_path` reads pool state (write-lock freed after reading), `solve_path` is pure compute (no lock needed), results are written back under write-lock.

3. **Copy-on-write results** — `latest_results()` returns a clone of results under the lock, then Python processes the clone lock-free. This is already partially the case (Python reads results via the unbounded channel, not `latest_results`).

## Assessment

This is an architectural change. The current design is correct — the lock guards against concurrent mutation. The question is whether lock hold time is actually causing latency in practice. If Python's hot loop only reads from the unbounded channel (not `latest_results`), then lock contention is minimal. Worth measuring before committing to a refactor.

data.title: Anchor legacy BlockPump::spawn against subscribe-phase block number
data.body:
## Goal
- Stop the legacy `BlockPump::spawn` from entering `run_with_stream` with an unanchored `current_block = 0`, which causes out-of-order log application against DB-snapshot-seeded engine state.

## Context
- Critical-review item #10.
- `rust/src/bot_core/block_pump.rs:120-176` (`spawn` legacy) seeds `SubscribeState{first_block: 0, …}` and ignores the subscribe-phase block number. `run_with_stream(combined, /*first_observed_block=*/0)` then sees `current_block == 0` and skips the cold-start backfill branch at `:487` because `first_observed_block == 0`.
- The first WS log (e.g. `log_block=21_500_000`) jumps `current_block` straight to that number with no backfill, applying logs out-of-order against engine state seeded at the DB snapshot block, with `last_solved_block` cursors reset to 0.
- The modern `subscribe()` + `resume()` flow avoids this. The legacy entry is still reachable (tests, single-protocol deployments, possibly `PyUniswapArbEngine.spawn`-style callers).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decide: (a) delete the legacy `spawn` entry and migrate any callers to `subscribe + resume`; or (b) have `spawn` call `subscribe()` to obtain the real `first_block` before `run_with_stream`, instead of hardcoding `0`. Document in `rust/CONTEXT.md`.
- If kept, add a test asserting that `spawn` against a live-feed stub applies logs in block order with a backfill from snapshot_block+1 to first_ws_block-1, mirroring the modern flow's invariants.
- No test or path can reach `run_with_stream` with both `current_block == 0` and a huge first observed log block.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just lint-rust`

## Done

- **Fix** (`rust/src/bot_core/block_pump.rs` `spawn` legacy): the legacy `BlockPump::spawn` discarded the `subscribe()` result's `first_block` + `combined_stream` (hard-coded `first_block: 0` and re-subscribed a THIRD time for the resume stream). Replaced with reusing the `state` returned by `subscribe()`: passes the real `first_block` as `first_observed_block` (the defensive cold-start anchor for `run_with_stream` — the `current_block == 0 && first_observed_block > 0` branch is the fallback when the `on_drain` cursor is absent) and the subscribe-prepared `combined_stream` (subscribe() already re-subscribes once internally; a third re-subscribe opened a gap window + discarded the anchor). Kept the `on_drain(first_block)` empty-batch send (primary anchor, mirrors `SolveCoordinator::on_drain`).
- **Decision (b)** (per acceptance criteria): kept the legacy `spawn` entry (still reached from `PyUniswapArbEngine::start(rpc_url)` for single-protocol / test deployments; the production path uses `EngineRegistry.start()` → subscribe/backfill/resume and does NOT call `engine.start()`). The `start()` legacy convenience (no `backfill_from_snapshot`) is preserved by design; documented in `rust/CONTEXT.md` (new `**BlockPump::spawn (legacy)**` entry).
- **Tests** (`block_pump::tests`, characterization Red→Green via the VTWCIG `for_test`/`run_test_loop` seam):
  - `cold_start_anchors_to_first_observed_block` — pins the cold-start branch honors `first_observed_block` when `last_processed_block()` is `None` (the defensive anchor the fix passes instead of `0`).
  - `legacy_spawn_processes_blocks_in_order_anchored_at_subscribe_block` — mimics spawn's `on_drain(W)` + `first_observed=W` and asserts W→W+1→W+2 in-order finalization (no out-of-order jump from 0).
  - `FakeDrainSink::on_drain` now faithfully advances the cursor (`last_processed_block`) — mirrors `SolveCoordinator::on_drain` so the test seam reproduces spawn's anchoring side-effect.
- **Validation gates**: `just lint-rust` clean; `just test-rust` 550 lib + 14 + 9 + 1, 0 failed (block_pump::tests 10 passed, +2 new). `tests/arbitrage/test_engine_registry_start.py` + `tests/rust/` 203 passed.

- Committed `d00c2e16` (single commit, code+tests+CONTEXT.md).

Result: rust/src/bot_core/block_pump.rs

data.title: Slice 10: UniswapEngine lock unification onto shared Arc<RwLock<Bot>>
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-408eb2c1`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `engine`, `lock-unification`, `deferred`, `closes-9356aaf7`, `slice-10`

---

**Slice 10 of the Polars three-layer migration (ADR-005, deferred target).** Master: `TODO-7e24d695`. Deps: slice 9 (V4 companion; engine path understood). **Closes open TODO `9356aaf7`** ("Eliminate Python pool mutable state for engine-managed pools").

**Goal.** Unify `UniswapEngine` onto the SAME `Arc<RwLock<Bot>>` as `PyBot` — one Rust-owned `Bot`, the engine pump + Python companions both read/write through it. Eliminates dual-state for engine-managed pools: the Python companion now reads LIVE engine-updated state (`9356aaf7`'s payoff).

**Rust.**
- `UniswapEngine.core: Arc<Mutex<Bot>>` → `Arc<RwLock<Bot>>` shared with `PyBot`.
- Resolve the nested lock-ordering question (ADR-005 Deferred): engine-then-core currently `Mutex`-then-`Mutex`; collapsing to one shared core lock, OR a documented alternative discipline. Lock order when nested stays engine-then-core; Python-facing `PyBot` methods take core alone and never call into the engine (the rule keeping the deadlock surface empty — ADR-003).
- `PyUniswapArbEngine` constructed WITH the shared `Arc`: needs a `PyBot` method to hand out the underlying `Arc` (or the engine is constructed FROM the `PyBot`/`Bot`).
- Spawned pump writes to the shared `Bot`; Python companions read live.

**Python.** `Bot` constructs the shared `PyBot` and passes the `Arc`/handle to `UniswapArbEngine`; Python subscribes to `newHeads` for fee/nonce only; results read from the engine channel.

**Tests.** `9356aaf7` acceptance; backrun-path tests (pump updates → companion reads live state, no stale reads); lock-deadlock surface tests; concurrent reader/writer tests under free-threading assumptions.

**Consistency at boundary.** Engine-managed pools' companions read live state (dual-state eliminated). `UniswapArbEngine` backrun path stays green. **RISKIEST slice** (lock semantics across the engine + Python) — execute with red/green TDD around the deadlock surface; do not collapse without characterizing the current engine-then-core `Mutex` invariant first.

**Acceptance.** `cargo`/`ruff`/`ty` green; `9356aaf7` closed; backrun-path tests + companion-live-read tests pass; no deadlock regressions (stress test the pump+read interleaving).

data.title: Revert exception swallowing in build_paths and fix RPC overload root cause
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-53b7453b`

**tags:** `bot`, `memory`, `rust`

## Done

- **Rust seam** (`rust/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine/py_binding.rs`): replaced the flat `VerifyError::Snapshot | Provider → PyRuntimeError` seam with two distinct `create_exception!` types sublassing `RuntimeError` — `VerificationMismatchError` (`VerifyError::Snapshot`, genuine on-chain mismatch — fatal) and `VerificationRpcError` (`VerifyError::Provider`, RPC/transport/provider-construction failure). `VerifyError::NoSnapshotStream` stays `PyRuntimeError` (programmer error). Registered both in the `degenbot_rs` module (`rust/src/lib.rs`) and re-exported from the engine module.
- **Python revert** (`examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`): the `build_paths` `except RuntimeError` block now classifies by `isinstance` instead of fragile `\"tick data mismatch\"` string matching. `VerificationMismatchError` and `VerificationRpcError` both crash loudly (raise); the swallowing of RPC failures is reverted. A narrow `except RuntimeError` still skips genuinely non-verification runtime errors (e.g. phase violations) for path-skip continuity.
- **Stubs** (`src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi`): added `VerificationMismatchError` / `VerificationRpcError` class stubs + `__all__` entries (so ty resolves them without per-line `# type: ignore`; no new ty diagnostics introduced vs clean HEAD).
- **Tests** (`tests/rust/test_verification_exceptions.py`, Red→Green): 6 tests asserting both types are exported, subclass RuntimeError, are DISTINCT types (so isinstance discrimination works), carry their messages, and are caught by a broad `except RuntimeError` handler (backward-compat). Verified Red (ImportError) before adding the types, Green after.
- **Validation gates**: `just lint-rust` clean; `just test-rust` 544 lib + 9 doctest + others, 0 failed. `tests/rust/test_verification_exceptions.py` 6 passed. `uv run ty check examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` introduces no new diagnostics (the pre-existing 60 ty diagnostics are unrelated pyo3-stub incompleteness).-

- **Bounded scope note**: per-call RPC transport failures inside `liquidity_verifier` are currently folded into `VerifyError::Snapshot` (hence `VerificationMismatchError`) — conflating them with genuine mismatches. The deeper refactor to separate them into a dedicated `VerifyError::Rpc` variant (so `VerificationRpcError` can drive a retry/backoff policy per option 1 of this task) is filed as follow-up `VP42BP` under epic NIMB23.

- Committed `4300172f` (code+tests) — single commit.

Result: rust/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine/py_binding.rs + rust/src/lib.rs + rust/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine/mod.rs + src/degenbot/degenbot_rs.pyi + examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py + tests/rust/test_verification_exceptions.py

data.title: Consolidate bot startup to one canonical path
Slice 3: lift EngineRegistry + HopInfo family into the library
data.body:
## Goal
- Lift the canonical engine-orchestration machinery (`EngineRegistry` + its cohesive engine-facing `HopInfo` family) out of the backrun example into `degenbot.arbitrage`, so the library itself owns the one correct way to start the bot.

## Context
- Plan 102 slice 3. Scope is B-MID (lift engine-operation machinery, not deployment policy). `EngineRegistry` (the subscribe→stream→backfill→verify ritual + register_v2/v3/v4 key maps + register_path) currently lives in examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py:724; tests import it via `import examples.eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust as runner`.
- Cohesive deps that MUST lift alongside (they're engine-facing hop descriptors, distinct from the SOLVER's `degenbot.arbitrage.optimizers.hop_types::HopType`/`degenbot.types.hop_types`):  `V2HopInfo`/`V3HopInfo`/`V4HopInfo`/`HopInfo`/`PathInfo`/`build_hops_from_pools` (examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py). All read only pool attributes — general, not deployment-specific.
- The lifted `register_v4_pool` carries NO Python pre-check (deleted in slice 2 — relies on the typed Rust exception).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Create `src/degenbot/arbitrage/engine_registry.py` (lifted `EngineRegistry`) + `src/degenbot/arbitrage/hop_info.py` (lifted `V2HopInfo`/`V3HopInfo`/`V4HopInfo`/`HopInfo`/`PathInfo`/`build_hops_from_pools`). COPY, do not move yet (the example keeps its local copies this slice — duplicated, still working; slice 4 deletes them).

data.title: Path-composition rejection predicate (token denylist / hop-count / min-liquidity)
data.body:
## Goal

Add a general **path-composition rejection predicate** so a bot can refuse an
`ArbitragePath`/`EngineRegistry.register_path` candidate by *policy*, not just
by engine admission. Rejections surface as a typed `PathRejectedError` (or a
small family) so callers classify by type, mirroring the `7SSOJX` /
Plan-102 typed-exception pattern now used for pool admission + verification.

## Context

Filed as the follow-up referenced in **Plan 102** (Consolidate bot startup).
Plan 102 slice 2 removed the V4 double-filter by lifting pool admission
(hooked/dynamic-fee refusal) into typed Rust exceptions — that did NOT need a
predicate, because admission is a *correctness floor* enforced in the Rust
core (the solver's CL math assumes no hook intervention + fixed fee). This
task is the distinct, *policy*-layer concern: composing/accepting a path by
deployment rules.

## Scope (path-COMPOSITION policy, distinct from Rust pool-admission)

- Token denylists / allowlists (intermediate + profit tokens)
- Hop-count policy (min/max stops)
- Min-liquidity gates
- (Possibly) duplicate-pool / self-loop guards

## Non-goals

- Pool admission stays in Rust (`BotState::register_v4_pool` →
  `HookedPoolRejectedError` / `DynamicFeePoolRejectedError`). Do NOT move it
  to a Python predicate — ADR-005 standalone-core constraint (a no-Python
  Rust consumer must be protected from hooked/dynamic-fee pools).

## Open design questions

- Predicate location: Python-side `degenbot.arbitrage` (where
  `EngineRegistry.register_path` lives) vs. a pluggable strategy object the
  caller injects (mirrors `ApprovalStrategy` / `PayloadComposer`).
- Types: one `PathRejectedError(ValueError)` with a reason enum, or a family
  (`TokenDenylistedError`, `HopCountExceededError`, `InsufficientLiquidityError`).

Plan: 102 (follow-up)

data.title: Preserve per-Swap priors across same-block multi-swap reorg rollback
data.body:
## Goal
- Reverse-apply V3/V4 Swap deltas correctly when a pool has multiple Swap events in the same block, so restoring to before that block lands on the true pre-block state.

## Context
- Critical-review item #5.
- `rust/src/bot_core/state_history.rs:207-220` `push_delta` replaces the newest delta when `delta.block() == newest.block()` ("same-block replacement"). For V3/V4, deltas are *partial* (each carries only its own priors); the second same-block Swap replaces the first Swap's delta, so the recorded `scalar_priors` become post-first-Swap, not pre-block.
- On `restore_before_block(B)`, the single popped block-B delta returns `scalar_priors` post-first-Swap → `state` lands on post-first-Swap instead of pre-block.
- V2 dodges this because each delta carries the full before/after transition record (`*_after` of the previous delta == pre-block state). The V3/V4 partial-delta store is incompatible with same-block replacement as written.
- Multiple same-block swaps on mainnet V3/V4 pools are common (multi-hop arb bots, MEV activity within a block).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Decide and implement one of: (a) stop collapsing same-block deltas — keep a per-block chain of partials, restore by reverse-applying them in order; or (b) coalesce same-block partial deltas into one delta whose `scalar_priors` is the *earliest* pre-block state and whose `tick_priors` accumulates *all* modified ticks (oldest-wins de-dupe already exists at `state_history.rs:~440`). Document the choice in the delta's docstring.
- Test: register a V3 pool, push two Swap deltas at block B (different scalars), then `restore_before_block(B+1)` and assert the pool scalars match pre-B state, not post-first-Swap.
- The V2 same-block semantics must be preserved (it currently special-cases the full-state transition correctly).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just lint-rust`

data.title: Slice 7: DEX subclass collapse (stance B) — LiquidityPool + DexIdentity
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-38f34cf3`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `stance-b`, `v2`, `breaking`, `slice-7`

**pi id:** `TODO-38f34cf3`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `stance-b`, `v2`, `breaking`, `slice-7`

---

**Slice 7 of the Polars three-layer migration (ADR-005).** Master: `TODO-7e24d695`. Deps: slice 4, 5 (V2 companion fully delegates), slice 6 (`DexIdentity`).

**Goal.** Collapse the hollow DEX-class hierarchy (stance B) into the generalized `LiquidityPool` companion carrying `dex: DexIdentity` data + strategy mixins for the two genuine behavioral DEXes (Camelot solidly-stable calc, Aerodrome log decoder). `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool`. **Public API break — accepted (0.x major refactor, user-confirmed).** No back-compat layer per AGENTS.md.

**Design decision (slice-7).** Builder resolves `DexIdentity` preset → unfolded `register_v2_pool` params (keeps `PyBot.register_v2_pool` signature stable). Strategy behavior keyed on `dex.variant`. Per-DEX strategy objects (`CamelotPoolCalc` solidly-stable, Aerodrome `_decode_aerodrome_v2_sync` decoder) wire the pre-wired `_calc_tokens_out_fn` / log handler from `DexVariant`.

**Python.**
- NEW generalized `LiquidityPool` companion (rename of `UniswapV2Pool` or new class) wrapping `PyLiquidityPool` + `dex: DexIdentity`.
- Strategy mixins: `CamelotPoolCalc` (solidly-stable) + Aerodrome decoder become strategy objects keyed on `dex.variant`.
- DELETE `SushiswapV2Pool`, `PancakeswapV2Pool`, `SwapbasedV2Pool`, `CamelotLiquidityPool`, `AerodromeV2Pool` (no back-compat aliases per AGENTS.md "design standalone features without a backwards compatibility layer"). Their tests become `LiquidityPool` + preset tests.

**Builders / Pool Type Registry.** `V2PoolBuilder` (+ collapsed `AerodromeV2Builder`/`CamelotBuilder`) resolves `DexIdentity` preset from factory (Pool Type Registry maps `(chain_id, factory) → DexIdentity`/`DexVariant`, not `→ class`) + constructs `LiquidityPool` with the right strategy. Per-DEX self-registration (`pool_type_registry.register()`) updates from class→identity.

**Registries.** `PoolRegistry` stores `LiquidityPool`. `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool` for all V2-family.

**Tests.** Rewrite DEX-subclass tests as `LiquidityPool` + preset tests. Camelot stable / Aerodrome stable behavior tests stay (via strategy). V2 calc tests stay (unchanged).

**Consistency at boundary.** BREAKING — callers doing `isinstance(pool, SushiswapV2Pool)` break (documented; 0.x). `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool` for all V2-family. Camelot/Aerodrome stable calc behavior preserved via strategy. All V2-family tests pass.

**Acceptance.** `cargo`/`ruff`/`ty` green; DEX-subclass tests rewritten + pass; Camelot/Aerodrome stable strategy tests pass; `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool`; `isinstance` calls audited + breaking change documented in a migration guide.

---

## Slice 7 — PARTIAL DONE (step 1 + step 2 landed; the collapse is remaining work)

Stopped at a clean green intermediate. The slice is NOT complete — only the rename + the Rust constructor foundation landed. The actual DEX subclass collapse (the breaking core of this slice) is the remaining bulk.

### Landed commits (green, self-contained)

- **`0b4a20e0` step 1 — rename `UniswapV2Pool` → `LiquidityPool`** (file + class + docs). Pure mechanical rename — no behavior change. Per ADR-005's layer-naming rule, the V2 companion shares the bare noun `LiquidityPool` with its wrapper `PyLiquidityPool` (V3/V4 keep their versioned names pending their own companion slices). 68 files updated via word-boundary sed (kept `UniswapV2PoolTracker`/`State`/`Calc`/`SwapAmounts`/`SimulationResult` untouched — they have their own names). 675 tests pass. Foundation for the collapse.

- **`94c3f9e4` step 2 — `PyDexIdentity #[new]` Python constructor** (+ pyi signature + 2 tests). Adds a `PyDexIdentity(factory, init_hash, fee_token0, fee_token1, variant, reserves_abi=None)` constructor so Python tests + builders can construct a custom `DexIdentity` view from explicit args. Mirrors Polars' builder pattern — presets remain the canonical resolution path (`dex_identity(variant)`) but custom identities are constructable for tests / ad-hoc deployments with arbitrary factory addresses. This is foundational for the collapse — `make_v2_pool` + the builders will construct a `DexIdentity` per-pool + pass to `LiquidityPool(dex=...)`. Without the Python constructor, custom identities couldn't be built (slice 6 exposed only preset resolution). 11 `TestDexIdentityPresets` tests + Rust 481 tests green.

### Remaining (the actual collapse — steps 3+; a focused multi-commit undertaking)

**Step 3 (non-breaking foundation — additive `dex` plumbing):**
- `LiquidityPool.__init__` accepts `dex: DexIdentity | None = None` additive param; when provided, `factory`/`init_hash`/`deployer`/`fee_token0/1` defaults come from the preset (explicit overrides take precedence — preserves the existing call shape). Subclasses + `make_v2_pool` continue to work without `dex` (explicit params only).
- `pool_type_registry.register(..., dex_identity: DexIdentity | None = None)` + `_RegistryEntry.dex_identity` + new `get_v2_identity(chain, factory) -> DexIdentity | None`.
- 5 DEX `__init__.py` self-reg sites pass `dex_identity=<preset>` (UNISWAP_V2 / SUSHISWAP_V2 / PANCAKESWAP_V2 / SWAPBASED_V2 / CAMELOT_V2_VOLATILE-for-factory-default — Camelot registers the volatile as factory-default; the builder resolves the per-pool stable flag on-chain + uses CAMELOT_V2_STABLE preset when stable).
- V2 + Camelot builders resolve `dex` from registry + pass `dex=` to `LiquidityPool(...)`.
- Fold `CamelotPoolCalc._calculate_tokens_out_from_tokens_in_stable_swap` + `_wire_camelot_calculations` stable-strategy seam INTO `LiquidityPool` (keyed off `stable_swap` flag, like today). Keep `CamelotPoolCalc` as the strategy mixin (or delete if all callers move to `LiquidityPool` directly — depends on whether subclasses survive step 3).
- New test for `get_v2_identity` returning the right presets.

**Step 4 (the breaking collapse):**
- Delete the 4 V2 subclass files: `sushiswap/pools.py` (keep V3), `pancakeswap/pools.py` (keep V3), `swapbased/pools.py` (delete entirely), `camelot/pools.py` (delete entirely).
- Delete `camelot/v2_pool_calc.py` (CamelotPoolCalc folded into `LiquidityPool`).
- Delete `swapbased/trackers.py` + Sushi/Pancake/Swapbased V2 trackers; rewrite the DEX `__init__.py` exports.
- Delete `CamelotBuilder` (fold its `build` fetches into `V2PoolBuilder.build` as a `if dex.variant in (CamelotV2Volatile, CamelotV2Stable): do_camelot_fetches()` branch — Camelot does 4 on-chain calls: `stableSwap()`, `FEE_DENOMINATOR()`, `token0FeePercent()`, `token1FeePercent()`). `CamelotBuilder.update` was functionally identical to `V2PoolBuilder.update` (just reserves fetch + `external_update`) — delete + use MRO fall-through to `LiquidityPool → v2_builder`.
- Builder dispatch: `Bot.register_builder(CamelotLiquidityPool, self._camelot_builder)` deleted; `register_builder(LiquidityPool, self._v2_builder)` handles all V2-family builds. `pool_class_for_descriptor` returns `LiquidityPool` for all V2-family (no more per-DEX class).
- `__init__.py` exports: remove `SushiswapV2Pool`/`PancakeswapV2Pool`/`SwapbasedV2Pool`/`CamelotLiquidityPool`. `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool` for all V2-family.
- `isinstance` audit: the 4 class names appear in `tests/test_async_bot.py:181`, `tests/registry/test_pool_subclass_selection.py:60,78`, `tests/builders/test_from_chain.py:161,176,231,232`, `tests/types/test_abc_abstract_properties.py:10,15,71,72,73,92,93`, `tests/types/test_concrete_pool_construction.py:15,154,169,259,402,414`, `tests/registry/test_pool_type_registry.py`, `tests/registry/test_pool_type_registry_singleton.py`, `tests/registry/test_full_exchange_registration.py` — these tests need rewriting as `LiquidityPool` + preset tests (the `variant` ClassVar moves to `dex.variant`; `issubclass(PancakeswapV2Pool, UniswapV2Pool)` becomes `pool.dex.variant == "pancakeswap-v2"`).
- Migration guide at `docs/migration-guides/dex-subclass-collapse.md` documenting the API break (0.x; no back-compat aliases per AGENTS.md): `isinstance(pool, SushiswapV2Pool)` → `pool.dex.variant == "sushiswap-v2"` (or `isinstance(pool, LiquidityPool)` for V2-family); `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool` for Sushi/Pancake/Swapbased/Camelot; deleted class names stop being importable.

**Acceptance (to verify when step 4 lands):** cargo/ruff/ty green; the 4 subclass tests rewritten as `LiquidityPool` + preset tests pass; Camelot stable strategy tests pass via the folded `LiquidityPool` method; `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool` for all V2-family (incl. the 4 former DEX subclasses); `isinstance` calls audited + migration guide documents the break.

### Status / recommendation

Slice 7 ≈ 20% done (foundational rename + Rust constructor). The collapse (steps 3+4) is the bulk — genuinely a **multi-commit undertaking** (similar scope to slice 4's 4 commits + 75 construction conversions + the test pyramid, but with the added complexity of a registry API change + factory-keyed builder routing + a migration guide). Recommend a focused follow-up session (fresh context) for steps 3 + 4 with careful TDD — the deep survey done here (`camelot/pools.py`, `camelot/v2_pool_calc.py`, `pool_type_registry.py`, `v2_builder_base.py`, `type_resolution.py:pool_class_for_descriptor`, `Bot._builder_for_pool` MRO walk, the `isinstance` audit list above) carries over; the new session can jump straight to the constructor refactor + the deletions.

---

## Slice 7 — step 3 DONE (`eecc7d91`) — additive `dex` plumbing landed

Non-breaking foundation complete: the registry + `LiquidityPool` + `make_v2_pool` + `V2PoolBuilder` + the 5 V2 DEX self-registration sites all carry `DexIdentity` now. The 4 hollow subclasses + `CamelotLiquidityPool` are untouched (their `variant` ClassVars still exist); `dex` rides alongside as additive metadata. All gates green; 654 tests pass; zero regressions (the 9 `test_from_chain`/`test_async_v2_builder` failures are pre-existing at the step-2 commit — unrelated to step 3).

### Landed commit `eecc7d91` — "feat: DexIdentity plumbing for V2 pools (ADR-005 slice 7 step 3)"

**Registry (`src/degenbot/registry/pool_type.py`):**
- `register(..., dex_identity: PyDexIdentity | None = None)` — new optional kwarg; `_RegistryEntry.dex_identity: PyDexIdentity | None = None`.
- `get_v2_identity(chain_id, factory) -> PyDexIdentity | None` — resolves the preset; returns `None` for unregistered OR registered-without-dex (Aerodrome V2 — deferred per `TODO-e30504ed`).

**Companion (`src/degenbot/uniswap/liquidity_pool.py`):**
- `__init__` gains `dex: PyDexIdentity | None = None`. When provided AND `factory`/`init_hash`/`deployer_address`/`fee_token0`/`fee_token1` are `None`, the preset fills them in. Explicit params always win (non-breaking — existing callers pass all explicit params).
- `self.dex = dex` — the metadata attribute step 4 collapses the `variant` ClassVar onto.
- `factory`/`fee_token0`/`fee_token1` now default to `None` (were required); raises `DegenbotValueError` if `factory` can't be resolved from either explicit or `dex`.
- **Fee conversion at the boundary:** `dex.fee_token0 = (gamma_numer, fee_denom)` (retained post-fee fraction, Rust convention — slice 5); the companion stores the FEE `Fraction` → `Fraction(fee_denom - gamma_numer, fee_denom)` (e.g. preset `(997, 1000)` → `Fraction(3, 1000)`). The module doc + conversion code bake the slice-5 convention in explicitly.

**5 DEX self-reg sites** (`src/degenbot/{uniswap,sushiswap,pancakeswap,swapbased,camelot}/__init__.py`): each imports `dex_identity` from `degenbot_rs`, resolves the canonical preset once (`uniswap_v2_identity = dex_identity("uniswap-v2")` etc.), asserts non-None, passes `dex_identity=<preset>` to `register()`. For the loop-based ones (uniswap/sushi/pancake) the preset is resolved once before the loop (it's the same across chains — `variant`/`reserves_abi`/`init_hash`/default-fees are chain-independent; the per-chain factory is in the registry key, not the preset). Camelot registers `camelot-v2-volatile` as the factory default (step 4 adds the builder's on-chain stable-flag → `camelot-v2-stable` switch).

**V2PoolBuilder** (`src/degenbot/builders/v2_pool_builder.py`): `dex = pool_type_registry.get_v2_identity(chain_id, common.factory)` alongside the existing `get_v2_class`; passes `dex=dex` to the companion. The 3 hollow subclasses inherit the new param (they don't override `__init__`). `CamelotBuilder`'s `dex` wiring defers to step 4 (its `CamelotLiquidityPool.__init__` is overridden + doesn't forward `dex` — folds when the subclass is deleted).

**`make_v2_pool`** (`tests/helpers/v2_pool_factory.py`): accepts `dex=None`; fills in `factory`/`fee_token0/1`/`init_hash` from the preset when explicit params are `None`; threads `dex=`. For Rust registration, reads `(gamma_numer, fee_denom)` directly from the preset when `dex` provided the fees (no `_gamma_complement` conversion — the preset is already the retained fraction).

**Tests** (`tests/registry/test_dex_identity_plumbing.py`, 17 new): Red→Green TDD.
- `TestRegistryDexIdentity` (4): register/get_v2_identity round-trip, None-when-no-preset, None-when-unregistered, independence from get_v2_class.
- `TestSingletonDexPresets` (parametrized × 7 + 2): cross-check that after `import degenbot`, each of the 5 DEX factories + multi-chain Uniswap/Sushi resolves the right preset via `get_v2_identity`; preset fields match slice-6 Rust constants; Aerodrome V2 correctly has NO `dex_identity` (deferred).
- `TestLiquidityPoolDexIdentity` (4): `LiquidityPool(dex=preset, no explicit factory/fees)` fills from preset; explicit overrides win; `dex is None` default; PancakeStyle 3-tuple `reserves_abi` via `dex`.

### Design notes for step 4

- The `dex.fee_token0 = (gamma_numer, fee_denom)` ↔ Python `fee_token0: Fraction` conversion is encapsulated in `LiquidityPool.__init__` + `make_v2_pool`. When step 4 deletes the subclasses, the builders + tests that today pass explicit `fee_token0=Fraction(...)` can switch to `dex=preset` + omit the fee (the preset provides it). The conversion stays at the `LiquidityPool` boundary.
- Camelot's stable-flag → preset switch is the one remaining builder-side concern for step 4: `CamelotBuilder.build` fetches `stable_swap` on-chain; when `stable_swap=True` it should resolve `dex_identity("camelot-v2-stable")` instead of the factory-default `camelot-v2-volatile`. This is a 3-line conditional in the (folded) V2 builder's Camelot branch.
- `CamelotPoolCalc` (the stable-strategy mixin) still folds into `LiquidityPool` in step 4 — step 3 did NOT fold it (it's coupled to deleting `CamelotLiquidityPool`, which inherits it; folding now would MRO-conflict).

### Status

Slice 7 ≈ 35% done (rename + Rust constructor + additive `dex` plumbing — 3 commits). The breaking collapse (step 4) is the remaining bulk: delete the 4 subclass files + `CamelotPoolCalc` + `CamelotBuilder`; fold Camelot's stable strategy + on-chain fetches into `V2PoolBuilder`; `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool`; `isinstance` audit across ~8 test files + migration guide at `docs/migration-guides/dex-subclass-collapse.md`.

---

## slice 7 — step 4 DONE (`d1e43e9` 4a + `bd1fff17` 4b + `6d1adcf9` lint) — the breaking collapse landed

The hollow V2 DEX subclass hierarchy is collapsed. `Bot.build_pool` returns `LiquidityPool` for every V2-family DEX (Uniswap/Sushi/Pancake/Swapbased/Camelot); DEX identity (variant tag, reserves ABI shape, default fees, factory/init-hash) lives on the registration + the canonical Rust `DexIdentity` preset — no per-DEX subclasses.

### step 4a — `d1e43e9d` "feat: fold Camelot stable strategy into LiquidityPool (slice 7 step 4a)"
Additive, non-breaking: `LiquidityPool` gains the Camelot solidly-stable calc (`_calculate_tokens_out_from_tokens_in_stable_swap`) + the stable `to_hop_state` branch (`SolidlyStableHop` with `calc_exact_in_stable`/`k_camelot`/`get_y_camelot`) + the `stable_swap`/`fee_denominator` class defaults + a `calculate_tokens_out_from_tokens_in` strategy override (stable → stable math; else `super()` → the slice-5 Rust delegation, unperturbed). 10 Red→Green parity/fold tests in `tests/uniswap/v2/test_liquidity_pool_camelot_fold.py`. The fold is behavior-identical to `CamelotPoolCalc` (validated by parity against a reference `CamelotLiquidityPool`). Surfaced a PRE-EXISTING bug — `calc_exact_in_stable` calls `get_y_func(x, xy, y, decimals0, decimals1)` (5 args) but `get_y_camelot` takes 3 → Camelot's stable `to_hop_state` branch is dead code (always `TypeError`). Tracked in **TODO-7ea2e7d9** (the direct stable CALC path is unaffected — it calls `k_camelot`/`get_y_camelot` directly with the right arity).

### step 4b — `bd1fff17` "feat: collapse hollow V2 DEX subclasses (slice 7 step 4b)"
Breaking (0.x; no back-compat aliases per AGENTS.md). The 31-file collapse:

- **registry** (`pool_type.py`): `register(..., variant: str | None = None)` override — takes precedence over `getattr(pool_class, "variant")`. Lets the canonical `LiquidityPool` (variant=None) register WITH `variant="sushiswap"` etc., preserving the DB `kind` ("sushiswap_v2") — keeps existing DB rows resolvable while collapsing the class hierarchy.
- **5 DEX self-reg sites**: each registers `LiquidityPool` + `variant="<dex>"` + `dex_identity=<preset>`. Camelot registers `camelot-v2-volatile` (factory default); the builder switches to `camelot-v2-stable` when on-chain `stableSwap()` is true.
- **V2PoolBuilder fold**: Camelot's 4 non-standard on-chain fetches + the stable-preset switch folded into `build` as a branch keyed on `dex_identity.variant.startswith("camelot-v2")`. New `_fetch_camelot_state` static helper + `CamelotStateFetch` dataclass mirroring the deleted `CamelotBuilder.build`.
- **deletions**: `swapbased/pools.py`, `swapbased/trackers.py`, `camelot/pools.py`, `camelot/v2_pool_calc.py` (`CamelotPoolCalc` folded 4a), `builders/camelot_builder.py`; V2 class bodies stripped from `sushiswap/pools.py`+`trackers.py` + `pancakeswap/pools.py`+`trackers.py` (V3 retained); V2 trackers (`SushiswapV2PoolTracker` etc.) removed → use `UniswapV2PoolTracker`; vacuumed all imports/exports + `Bot`/`AsyncBot` builder dispatch. DB table models (`{Sushiswap,Pancakeswap,Swapbased}V2PoolTable`) are KEPT — ORM persistence keyed by the preserved `kind`, orthogonal to the class collapse.
- **test rewrites** (offline-runnable, 6 files): `test_pool_type_registry.py` (variant is now a registration field, verified via `get_descriptor().variant` not a class ClassVar), `test_pool_type_registry_singleton.py` (V2 entries → `LiquidityPool`), `test_full_exchange_registration.py` (registrations table V2 → `LiquidityPool`; fixture passes `variant=`), `test_abc_abstract_properties.py` (per-DEX V2 shape tests consolidated into one `LiquidityPool` test), `test_concrete_pool_construction.py` (helpers + parametrize + inheritance → `LiquidityPool`), `test_builder_update_staticmethod.py` (drops `CamelotBuilder` from the conformance matrix), `test_uniswap_trackers.py` (`SushiswapV2PoolTracker` → `UniswapV2PoolTracker`), `test_liquidity_pool_camelot_fold.py` (4a transitional parity tests deleted; direct fold regression tests retained).
- **fork tests module-skipped** (4 files, anvil-gated, premise tied to deleted subclasses): `test_from_chain.py`, `test_pools.py`(pancake), `test_pool_subclass_selection.py`, `test_uniswap_v2_liquidity_pool.py`. Each `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=True)` pointing to the migration guide. Pending a focused follow-up anvil rewrite to the `LiquidityPool` + `dex.variant` model.
- **migration guide**: `docs/migration-guides/dex-subclass-collapse.md` — documents the API break (`isinstance(pool, SushiswapV2Pool)` → `pool.dex.variant == "sushiswap-v2"`; `Bot.build_pool` → `LiquidityPool` for all V2-family; import/tracker migration; fork-test-pending-rewrite section; the pre-existing `get_y_camelot` arity bug).

### step 4c — `6d1adcf9` "lint(python): fix pre-existing tests/ formatter drift"
Incidental: `ruff format src/ tests/` (run during 4b) caught ~39 files of pre-existing tests/ formatter drift (fmt-check-python only gates `src/`); pure formatter-driven, no behavior change. Split into its own `lint` commit per commitlint conventions.

Full offline suite: **ZERO NEW failures** (step-4a baseline 34 failures → 4b 24; the 24 are all pre-existing — fork fixtures lacking anvil nodes, README doctest staleness, builder-context/pickle flakes). 3062 tests pass; 2942 of those are the collapse-relevant pyramid + the rewritten tests (all green).

data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-6918d983`

**tags:** `encoding`, `compact-commands`, `gas-optimization`, `P2`

**pi id:** `TODO-6918d983`

**tags:** `encoding`, `compact-commands`, `gas-optimization`, `P2`

---

## Summary
Partially done: V3_SWAP_DELTA and ERC20_XFER_BALANCE are now importable but not yet used in path encoders.

### What's Available
- `enc_v3_swap_delta(pool_idx, zfo, recipient_idx)` — 4 bytes. Reads amount from PM exttload (amount owed to V3 pool from callback params). Only usable when V3 is inside a V4 unlock and the owed amount is deterministically known from the callback.
- `enc_erc20_xfer_balance(token_idx, recipient_idx)` — 3 bytes. Transfers executor's entire balance of a token. Useful for sweep operations.

### Why Not Used Yet
- V3_SWAP_DELTA: The current V3 encoders use V3_SWAP_COMPACT with explicit amounts. V3_SWAP_DELTA reads from PM exttload, which requires the V3 swap to be inside a V4 unlock context. Most V3 swaps happen outside V4 unlock (they're triggered by V3 callbacks), so V3_SWAP_DELTA has limited applicability. The only case where V3 is inside V4 unlock is in V4→V3 paths, but those already use V3_SWAP_COMPACT with the amount from the forward token output.

- ERC20_XFER_BALANCE: Replacing `enc_erc20_transfer(token_idx, recipient_idx, amount)` (15 bytes) with `enc_erc20_xfer_balance(token_idx, recipient_idx)` (3 bytes) saves 12 bytes per call, but is only safe when the executor's entire balance of that token should be sent. For flash loan repayments, the exact amount matters (not the full balance). For profit sweeps after all swaps, the exact amount is also usually known.

### When to Use
- V3_SWAP_DELTA: Inside V4 unlock when V3's input amount is from callback delta
- ERC20_XFER_BALANCE: When sweeping remaining balance after all operations are done (e.g., WETH flash repayment when the executor holds exactly the right amount)

data.title: Migrate Bot/PoolRegistry to wrap Rust-core PyPool handles (BotCore peer to UniswapEngine, ADR-003 follow-up)
data.body: **pi id:** `TODO-69cc2bea`

**pi id:** `TODO-69cc2bea`

---

## Context

ADR-003 (`docs/adr/ADR-003-botcore-state-layer.md`) settled the **state-and-concerns** architecture: `BotCore` is the single Rust owner of pool/token state, peer to `UniswapEngine` (which owns solving + the pump). That ADR deliberately did **not** decide how the Python `Bot` session class and its three registries migrate to wrap the new Rust-core handles. This todo tracks that follow-up session.

## Out of scope for ADR-003, in scope here

Today's Python `Bot` (`src/degenbot/bot.py`) owns:
- `ConnectionManager` (RPC providers) — I/O, stays Python
- `DatabaseSessionManager` — I/O, stays Python
- `PoolRegistry` (`Address → Python AbstractLiquidityPool`) — **migrates**: pools now have Rust-owned state
- `TokenRegistry` (`Address → Python Erc20Token`) — **migrates**: tokens have Rust-owned metadata (ADR-003: `BotCore.tokens` + `PyToken` handle)
- `ManagedPoolRegistry` (V4, `(chain, PoolManager, PoolId) → Python pool`) — **migrates**
- Per-family builders (`V2Builder`, `V3Builder`, `V4Builder`, `BalancerBuilder`, `CamelotBuilder`, `CurvePoolBuilder`) — I/O orchestration, stay Python, but their *return values* shift to Rust handles

## The decision this session must make

**What does `Bot.build_pool` return under ADR-003's architecture?** Three resolutions identified during grilling (consult `ADR-003` for context):

| Option | `Bot.build_pool` returns | Registry holds | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **B1 — direct `PyPool`** | the Rust handle itself | `Address → PyPool` | cleanest long-term; breaks library consumers expecting `AbstractLiquidityPool` methods |
| **B2 — Python wrapper over `PyPool`** | thin Python class implementing `ArbitragePathPool`/`AbstractLiquidityPool` by delegating to `PyPool` | `Address → Python wrapper` | preserves library API; wrapper is stateless orchestration; **mirrors the `Erc20Token`-wraps-`PyToken` pattern ADR-003 settled for tokens** |
| **B3 — `PyPool` registered in `BotCore`, `Bot` registry removed** | `PyPool` | no Python `PoolRegistry` — `BotCore` is the registry | cleanest but biggest blast radius |

**Provisional recommendation from grilling: B2**, by direct analogy to the token pattern (`Erc20Token` wraps `PyToken`, keeps price oracle + display Python-side; the pool wrapper wraps `PyPool`, keeps subscription/publish Python-side if needed). But this needs revisiting against *real library callers* — don't commit before checking:
- who constructs `ArbitragePath(pools=[...])` and what pool types they pass
- whether `ArbitragePathPool`/`AbstractLiquidityPool` protocol surface is fully coverable by delegation to `PyPool`
- whether Python-side pool subscription (Pool State Messages) still has a role under ADR-003, or whether notification flows entirely through `UniswapEngine`'s result batches

## Related concepts (from ADR-003 grilling)

- **`PyPool`**: thin PyO3 handle over `Arc<Mutex<BotCore>>` + `pool_id`; reads state, exposes `calculate_tokens_out`/`calculate_tokens_in`/`encode_swap`. Under ADR-003 this is the Rust-core pool identity.
- **`PyToken`**: thin PyO3 handle over `Arc<Mutex<BotCore>>` + `Address`; reads token metadata (address, decimals, symbol, name). Python's `Erc20Token` wraps it with the price oracle.
- **`PoolRegistry`/`TokenRegistry`/`ManagedPoolRegistry`**: today class instances owned by `Bot`; under ADR-003 some/all may collapse into `BotCore`'s existing `pool_addresses` index.

## Prereqs

This session depends on ADR-003 being at least partially implemented (S1 — V2 state consolidation onto BotCore — should be done first, so `PyPool`/`PyBotCore` are real, working handles to wrap). Don't start before S1 lands.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Decision B1/B2/B3 recorded as an ADR (probably ADR-004 or similar)
- [ ] `Bot.build_pool`/`build_erc20token`/`build_managed_pool` return the chosen shape
- [ ] `PoolRegistry`/`TokenRegistry`/`ManagedPoolRegistry` either migrated or deleted per the decision
- [ ] `ArbitragePath` construction path verified against real library callers
- [ ] Production example (`examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`) `EngineRegistry` either still works or has a clean replacement (it currently builds Python pools and re-registers with the engine — ADR-003's `PyPool`-as-construction-entry should simplify this)

**Goal.** Split the single `rust/` crate into three, mirroring Polars exactly (`polars-core` / `polars-python` / `polars` umbrella):
- `degenbot-core` — `Bot`, `V2/V3/V4/Curve/BalancerPoolState`, `DexIdentity` + presets, calc math, reorg, event decoders. **Zero `pyo3` imports** (verified like Polars: `rg 'use pyo3' degenbot-core/src` = empty; the `polars-core` precedent found a declared-but-unused `pyo3` dep with 0 imports — degenbot-core must have neither).
- `degenbot-python` (name TBD) — all `*_py.rs` `#[pyclass]`/`#[pyfunction]` files: `py_bot.rs`, `py_liquidity_pool.rs`, `py_erc20_token.rs`, `py_binding.rs` (PyUniswapArbEngine), etc. All `pyo3` lives here.

**Acceptance.** `cargo`/`ruff`/`ty` green; standalone `degenbot-core` consumer test runs without Python; `rg 'use pyo3' degenbot-core/src` = empty; `degenbot_rs` import probe + full test suite green; `cargo add degenbot` umbrella re-exports `Bot`/`DexIdentity`/state structs with zero `pyo3`.

data.title: Test bot with all 27 pool version permutations using PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-f83d4d86`

**tags:** `arbitrage`, `testing`

**pi id:** `TODO-f83d4d86`

**tags:** `arbitrage`, `testing`

---

Goal: Systematically test each of the 27 three-hop pool version permutations (V2/V3/V4 × 3 hops) using the `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER` config and `pool_type_per_depth` DFS pruning. Identify encoding failures and fix them.

## The 27 permutations

| # | Permutation | Notes |
|---|-------------|-------|
| 1 | V2-V2-V2 | |
| 2 | V2-V2-V3 | |
| 3 | V2-V2-V4 | |
| 4 | V2-V3-V2 | |
| 5 | V2-V3-V3 | |
| 6 | V2-V3-V4 | |
| 7 | V2-V4-V2 | |
| 8 | V2-V4-V3 | |
| 9 | V2-V4-V4 | |
| 10 | V3-V2-V2 | |
| 11 | V3-V2-V3 | |
| 12 | V3-V2-V4 | |
| 13 | V3-V3-V2 | |
| 14 | V3-V3-V3 | |
| 15 | V3-V3-V4 | Reverse-order V3, V3b→PM |
| 16 | V3-V4-V2 | V3a→PM, V4_TAKE→V2c |
| 17 | V3-V4-V3 | V3c-reverse, currently all `transfer amount exceeds balance` (tax token) |
| 18 | V3-V4-V4 | |
| 19 | V4-V2-V2 | |
| 20 | V4-V2-V3 | V3c-reverse |
| 21 | V4-V2-V4 | V4_TAKE→V2b direct + V2_SWAP_CALC |
| 22 | V4-V3-V2 | V4_TAKE→V3b during callback |
| 23 | V4-V3-V3 | V4_TAKE→V3b (IIA ✓) |
| 24 | V4-V3-V4 | V4_TAKE→V3b during callback, sync+settle |
| 25 | V4-V4-V2 | |
| 26 | V4-V4-V3 | V4_TAKE→V3 during V3 callback |
| 27 | V4-V4-V4 | Delta netting, dynamic swap amounts |

## Permutation Verification Procedure

For each of the 27 permutations, run exactly this process:

### Step 1: Set the permutation filter

Edit `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER` in `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` to isolate one permutation:

```python
PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER: set[str] | None = {"V2-V3-V4"}  # one permutation at a time
```

This automatically:
- Loads only the required pool table types into the graph (via `_pool_types_from_filter`)
- Prunes DFS edges at each hop to enforce the permutation ordering (via `pool_type_per_depth`)

### Step 2: Restart the bot detached, capturing output to a log file

```bash
cd ~/code/degenbot
nohup uv run python examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py \
  > logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.pid
```

### Step 3: Observe for 15 minutes

Wait 15 minutes for sufficient blocks and simulation data. The bot will:
- Build paths matching only this permutation
- Solve them via the Rust engine
- Simulate profitable candidates via `eth_simulateV1`
- Log outcomes under `[sim]` (summary) and `[sim-fail]` (individual failures)

### Step 4: Report simulatability percentage

After 15 minutes, extract the results from the log:

```bash
# Total simulation candidates (from [sim] lines)
TOTAL=$(grep -c '\[sim\]' logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.log || echo 0)

# Successful simulations (gross profit > 0 = onchain-executable)
OK=$(grep '\[sim\]' logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.log | grep -oP '\d+ ok' | grep -oP '\d+' | paste -sd+ | bc || echo 0)

# Failed simulations (revert on simulation = encoding bug or on-chain state mismatch)
FAIL=$(grep '\[sim\]' logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.log | grep -oP '\d+ failed' | grep -oP '\d+' | paste -sd+ | bc || echo 0)

# Calculate simulatability rate
echo "Permutation V2-V3-V4: $OK ok / $TOTAL candidates ($(( OK * 100 / (OK + FAIL) ))% simulatable)"
```

A simulation that completes with a result (gross profit > 0 or even gross profit = 0 but no revert) counts as **onchain-executable** — the encoding is correct. A simulation that reverts counts as a **failure** — the encoding is wrong or the on-chain state doesn't match the solver's assumption. We don't require profit, only that the swap could execute onchain.

### Step 5: Classify and record

For each permutation, record:

| # | Permutation | Candidates | Simulatable | % | Classification | Failure modes |
|---|-------------|-----------|-------------|---|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | V2-V2-V2 | | | | ✅/⚠️/❌ | |

Classification:
- ✅ **Passing** — ≥80% simulatable. Remaining failures are tax-token reverts, liquidity edge cases, or rounding residuals.
- ⚠️ **Partial** — 20–79% simulatable. Some encoding bugs mixed with tax-token/liquidity failures.
- ❌ **Broken** — <20% simulatable. Encoding bug confirmed. Must debug and fix before re-testing.

### Step 6: Debug and fix broken/partial encoders

For ❌ and ⚠️ permutations:

1. Examine `[sim-fail]` lines for the revert reason (decoded selector, error string)
2. For V4 reverts: use `debug_traceCall` output (already logged at DEBUG level for V4-hybrid paths)
3. Cross-reference with the encoder function in `eth_backrun_helpers.py`
4. Compare against the contract test patterns in `~/code/executor/tests/`
5. Fix the encoder, re-test that single permutation
6. If the fix affects shared code (e.g., `enc_v4_settle_all`, `enc_v3_swap_compact`), re-test permutations that use that shared code

### Step 7: Kill the bot process and proceed to the next permutation

```bash
kill $(cat logs/perm-V2-V3-V4.pid)
```

Return to Step 1 with the next permutation.

## Known issues

- V3-V4-V3: all `Uni::_transferTokens: transfer amount exceeds balance` — ~0% success. Likely tax-token (0x1f9840 = UNI) but could also have encoder bugs. Need to test with non-tax-token paths specifically.
- V2 pool building via `bot.build_pool()` requires the init hash to be known. If V2 permutations produce 0 candidates, verify V2 pool tables have data in the DB and that `bot.build_pool()` can resolve V2 init hashes.

## Completed Infrastructure Changes

### Fix: Duplicate return in `_3hop_v3_v4_v2` encoder
- Removed unreachable `return enc_preamble(at) + commands` that followed the correct return statement in `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`

### Feature: Auto-derive `pool_types` from `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER`
- Added `_pool_types_from_filter()` helper in `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`
- When `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER` is set, `pool_types` is automatically derived from the version tags mentioned in the filter (e.g., `{"V2-V3-V4"}` → loads all V2+V3+V4 table types)
- When `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER` is `None`, all V2/V3/V4 table types are loaded (maximum coverage)
- Replaced hardcoded `pool_types=[UniswapV3PoolTable, UniswapV4PoolTable]` with `_pool_types_from_filter(PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER)`
- This unblocks all 27 permutations — V2 is no longer excluded from the graph
- Added pool types log line for observability
- Updated `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER` docstring to explain auto-derivation

### Verification
- All 27 permutations produce consistent `pool_types` / `pool_type_per_depth` sets
- `pool_types` is always a superset of the types in `pool_type_per_depth`
- Both modified files pass syntax checks
- `eth_backrun_helpers.py` imports cleanly with all 27 encoders

data.title: Slice 14: Stateful I/O struct PyBotIo — port provider/DB I/O to Rust
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-f9c4a115`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `pybot-io`, `io-port`, `deferred`, `rust`, `slice-14`

**pi id:** `TODO-f9c4a115`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `pybot-io`, `io-port`, `deferred`, `rust`, `slice-14`

---

**Slice 14 of the Polars three-layer migration (ADR-005, deferred target).** Master: `TODO-7e24d695`. Deps: slice 13 (crate split; `PyBotIo` lives in `degenbot-python`).

**Goal.** Port the stateful I/O (RPC provider / DB session) to Rust as a `#[pyclass]` `PyBotIo` (stateful, holds provider/DB refs), so the `Bot` orchestration can move to Rust. Per ADR-005, naming follows `Py + *Io`/`*Reader`. This is the last step toward a pure-Rust bot (a Rust consumer using `degenbot-core` + a Rust-native I/O struct — though `PyBotIo` itself is Python-facing; the standalone Rust I/O is a further step beyond this slice).

**Rust (new).** `degenbot-python` `bot_io.rs` (or `py_bot_io.rs`):
- `PyBotIo` `#[pyclass]` holding provider/DB handles (the `ProviderAdapter`/`DatabaseSessionManager` equivalents in Rust).
- Methods for the builder I/O choreography (DB lookup → RPC fetch → decode → construct) currently in Python builders' `build()`/`update()` — moved here, called from Python via `PyBotIo`.
- Reuses the existing `AsyncProviderAdapter`/`SyncProviderAdapter` Rust seams (the `provider/` module split).

**Python.** `Bot` delegates I/O to `PyBotIo` instead of doing it inline; the Python `Bot` shrinks to config + orchestration (which providers, which DBs, chain config, result dispatch). Builders' `build()`/`update()` become thin callers of `PyBotIo` methods (the I/O choreography moves; the construction logic — wrap-with-companion — stays Python until the pure-Rust-bot step).

**Tests.** I/O round-trip tests (DB pool lookup, ERC20 metadata RPC fetch, decode, construct-companion); provider/DB mock tests; the `PyBotIo` surface mirrors the `BuilderContext` dependencies (`db`/`erc20_builder`/`default_chain_id`/`managed_pools`).

**Consistency at boundary.** `Bot.build_pool` / `build_erc20token` / `build_managed_pool` end-to-end green via `PyBotIo` (same observable behavior). The pure-Rust-bot target becomes reachable (a Rust consumer using `degenbot-core` + a `PyBotIo`-equivalent Rust I/O struct — the standalone Rust I/O is a further step, not this slice).

## Goal
- Make `PyLiquidityPool.apply_swap` / `apply_liquidity_update` actually mutate V4 pools instead of silently routing into V3-only methods that no-op on V4 entries.

## Context
- Critical-review item #3.
- `rust/src/bot_core/py_liquidity_pool.rs:346` (`apply_swap`) and `:383` (`apply_liquidity_update`) call `apply_v3_swap_by_pool_id` / `apply_v3_liquidity_update_by_pool_id` unconditionally.

data.title: Eliminate Python pool mutable state for engine-managed pools
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-9356aaf7`

**tags:** `python`, `architecture`, `future`

**pi id:** `TODO-9356aaf7`

**tags:** `python`, `architecture`, `future`

---

Currently, Python pool objects (UniswapV2Pool, UniswapV3Pool, UniswapV4Pool) hold mutable state (reserves, tick data, sqrt price) that is duplicated in the Rust engine after registration. After registration, the Python pool goes stale — the Rust engine's pump updates its own copy every block while nobody reads the Python pool's mutable state.

In the future architecture where Rust is the sole state owner, Python pool objects used by the engine should become lightweight structs carrying only:
- Immutable metadata needed for swap encoding (addresses, fee, tick_spacing, pool_id, hook_address, pool_key)
- Registration data (fetched once via RPC, passed to `register_pool`, then discarded)

The mutable state slot should be eliminated from the Python side entirely for engine-managed pools.

**Tension identified**: The existing pure-Python architecture held all state in pool objects. The Rust engine approach makes Python the "operator" layer. This cleanup resolves the dual-state tension.

**Dependencies**: NOT on the critical path for rolling-start. Current dual-state works correctly (Python state is authoritative at registration time, then Rust takes over).

data.title: Distinguish per-call RPC transport failures from genuine mismatches in liquidity_verifier (7SSOJX follow-up)
data.body:
## Goal
- Distinguish per-call RPC transport failures from genuine tick-data mismatches inside `liquidity_verifier`, surfacing them as a dedicated `VerifyError::Rpc` → `VerificationRpcError` (Python) instead of folding both into `VerifyError::Snapshot`.

## Context
- Follow-up to `7SSOJX` (typed verification exceptions). That task introduced `VerificationMismatchError` (`VerifyError::Snapshot`) and `VerificationRpcError` (`VerifyError::Provider`, provider-construction) at the `py_binding` seam, and reverted the `build_paths` string-matching swallowing to type-based classification.
- **Remaining gap**: `rust/src/bot_core/liquidity_verifier.rs` wraps per-call RPC failures (`eth_call` / `call_v3_ticks` / `call_state_view_tick_liquidity`) as `VerificationMismatch { message: "... RPC call failed: {e}" }` — see e.g. `verify_v3_pool` (`liquidity_verifier.rs:~255`). These propagate to `VerifyError::Snapshot` → `VerificationMismatchError`, conflating a transient transport error with a genuine on-chain mismatch (both currently fatal).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Add a `VerifyError::Rpc(String)` variant (or reuse `Provider`) alongside `Snapshot`/`Provider`/`NoSnapshotStream` in `snapshot_verify.rs::VerifyError`.
- Refactor `liquidity_verifier` verification functions to return `Result<_, VerifyError>` (or a verifier-local error enum converting to `VerifyError`), mapping on-chain-mismatch → `Snapshot` and RPC transport failure → `Rpc` (NOT the current `.map_err(|e| VerificationMismatch { "... RPC call failed" })`).
- Update `EngineVerifyRpc` impls in `py_binding.rs` to propagate the `Rpc` variant (don't flatten to `Snapshot`), and `map_verify_err` to map `Rpc` → `VerificationRpcError`.
- `build_paths` then treats `VerificationRpcError` (per-call transport) as the retry/backoff candidate (option 1 of 7SSOJX) vs `VerificationMismatchError` (fatal). Decide retry-with-backoff policy + bound.
- Add Red/Green tests: a mock-provider verifier that returns a transport error surfaces `VerificationRpcError` (not `VerificationMismatchError`), and a genuine mismatch still surfaces `VerificationMismatchError`.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just lint-rust`
- `uv run pytest tests/rust/test_verification_exceptions.py`

data.title: Investigate architecture for Aerodrome-style V2 pools (solidly-stable + on-chain fees) in the three-layer model
data.body:
**pi id:** `TODO-e30504ed`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `aerodrome`, `architecture`, `investigation`, `deferred-from-slice-7`

**pi id:** `TODO-e30504ed`

**tags:** `polars-three-layer`, `adr-005`, `aerodrome`, `architecture`, `investigation`, `deferred-from-slice-7`

---

**Deferred from slice 7 (DEX subclass collapse).** Spun out per the user's call: Aerodrome is a unique design that may not collapse neatly into the V2 `LiquidityPool` companion; investigate architectural designs that more cleanly support this style of pool separately.

**Why Aerodrome doesn't fit the slice-7 collapse.** Unlike `SushiswapV2Pool`/`PancakeswapV2Pool`/`SwapbasedV2Pool` (hollow — just a `variant` ClassVar + `FEE`/`RESERVES_STRUCT_TYPES`) and `CamelotLiquidityPool` (a `UniswapV2Pool` subclass since slice 4, divergence = `CamelotPoolCalc` solidly-stable strategy + a `to_hop_state` branch), `AerodromeV2Pool` is **not a `UniswapV2Pool` subclass at all**. It's a fully-independent 564-line pure-Python pool — `class AerodromeV2Pool(PublisherMixin, PoolPickleMixin, AerodromeV2PoolStateMixin, AerodromeV2PoolCalc, AbstractLiquidityPool)` — with its own:
- State mixin (`AerodromeV2PoolStateMixin` + `AerodromeV2PoolState`), own `StateCache`, own `external_update`/`simulate_swap`/`simulate_swap_for_output`/`to_hop_state`/`build_swap_amount`.
- Own log decoder (`_decode_aerodrome_v2_sync`) + `LOG_HANDLERS`.
- Per-pool `stable: bool` flag (volatile vs stable pool — resolved on-chain via `stable()`; drives a solidly-stable-vs-constant-product calc branch).
- Per-pool on-chain `fee` (resolved via `factory.getFee(address, stable)` — not a DEX-wide constant; the preset carries only a typical default + the denominator).
- `get_pool_identity_values(...)` batch-fetches factory/token0/token1/stable/fee/reserves in one round-trip.
- `swap_is_viable` (state-level swap admissibility check) — not present on `UniswapV2Pool`.
- No `PyLiquidityPool` handle (deferred from slice 4's companion conversion — the slice-4 work that converted `UniswapV2Pool`/`CamelotLiquidityPool` to companions deliberately skipped Aerodrome).

**The architectural question.** The Polars three-layer companion (`PyLiquidityPool` + Rust `V2PoolState`) is a 2-token constant-product pattern. Aerodrome adds three things that don't fit:

1. **Solidly-stable-vs-constant-product duality.** A single pool is volatile OR stable (per-pool, on-chain). The stable path uses a different invariant (`calc_exact_in_stable` — same `solidly_stable` calculations module Camelot stable uses, but with default k/get_y vs Camelot's k_camelot/get_y_camelot). This isn't a DexIdentity preset problem — it's a pool-state-shape problem: the *same Rust `V2PoolState`* (reserves0/reserves1) backs both branches, but the calc dispatch is per-pool.
2. **On-chain fee resolution.** Fees aren't a DEX-wide constant — `factory.getFee(address, stable)` returns the per-pool fee at query time. The `DexIdentity` preset's `fee_token0/1` are "typical defaults," not the actual fee. Real fees must be fetched (builder I/O) and stored as pool state — not on the immutable `dex` identity. So `V2PoolState.fee_token0/1` (Rust) needs to be per-pool-mutable OR the companion carries the resolved fee Python-side.
3. **`get_pool_identity_values` batch fetch.** Aerodrome's identity isn't derivable from `(chain_id, factory)` alone — `stable()` + `factory.getFee(address, stable)` are per-pool reads. The registry's `(chain_id, factory) → class` (or `→ DexIdentity`) resolution doesn't close the loop; the builder must probe the pool on-chain to resolve (stable, fee, reserves) before construction.

**Candidate architectures to evaluate (this is the investigation's deliverable):**

- **A. Strategy-on-companion (minimal lift).** Convert Aerodrome to a `PyLiquidityPool` companion like Camelot: `LiquidityPool` (or an `AerodromeV2Pool` companion subclass) carries `stable: bool` + a resolved `fee` as Python-side pool state (set at construction from builder's on-chain `getFee` call), wires the solidly-stable calc strategy when `stable`. Rust `V2PoolState` keeps `fee_token0/1` as the resolved per-pool value (already mutable via `register_v2_pool`'s params). The `get_pool_identity_values` batch stays a builder concern. **Question to answer:** does this preserve the on-chain `getFee` parity + the stable calc + `swap_is_viable`?
- **B. Separate Rust state variant.** Like V3/V4 have their own `PoolEntry::V3`/`::V4`, Aerodrome could get `PoolEntry::SolidlyStableV2` — a variant holding reserves + stable flag + resolved fee + the k/get_y function pointers (or an enum selecting the solidly-stable flavor). Heavier Rust lift; cleaner separation; may be overkill if (A) holds.
- **C. Third-family framing.** Treat Aerodrome-V2 as the third "family" alongside Curve/Balancer (ADR-003's "third family"): a Solidly-invariant family that gets its own companion + own Rust state (when it warrants Rust backing). Matches the "third-family" language already in ADR-003/005.
- **D. Hybrid: companion + per-pool fee override.** Companion carries `dex: DexIdentity` (deployment identity — factory/deployer/init_hash, which IS DEX-wide) + a separate per-pool `fee: Fraction` + `stable: bool` resolved at construction. Strategy wired off `stable` (like Camelot). The preset's `fee_token0/1` are only fallbacks when the builder doesn't fetch (rare). **This is roughly what slice 7a's `LiquidityPool` will do for Camelot anyway** — so (A) and (D) converge.

**Deliverable.** A short design memo (in the Aerodrome CONTEXT.md or a new ADR) choosing one of A/B/C/D, with the trade-offs. Then implement as a follow-up slice to slice 7 (depends on slice-7's `LiquidityPool` + `DexIdentity` landing first — those are the foundation either way). NOT blocking slice 7 (slice 7 leaves Aerodrome untouched as its own class).

# Epic — sub-task tracker

Parent task tracking its sub-task completion.

---

**Goal.** Apply ADR-005 (Polars-Inspired Three-Layer Architecture) across the codebase: every Rust-owned stateful resource gets the `Bot core → Py* wrapper (Arc<RwLock/shared key) → Python companion` topology. Continues ADR-005 slices 1-2 (already landed: `name=` overrides dropped; `PyPool`→`PyLiquidityPool`, `PyToken`→`PyErc20Token`).

**Current state (post slices 1-2).**
- Rust core `Bot` (`rust/src/bot_core/mod.rs`) owns V2/V3/V4 state in `PoolEntry::{V2(V2PoolState), V3(V3PoolState), V4(V4PoolState)}` + `TokenEntry` map, reorg journals, swap math, swap encoding.
- `PyBot` (`py_bot.rs`) exposes: register/update/journal for V2+V3, `register_token`/`get_token`→`PyErc20Token`, `calculate_tokens_out/in`, `encode_swap`, `get_pool`→`PyLiquidityPool`. **No V4 register/update** (V4 registers via the engine path).
- `PyLiquidityPool` (`py_liquidity_pool.rs`): `calculate_tokens_out/in`, `encode_swap`, `pool_id` getter. **No read getters** (reserves/fee/tokens/factory) — needed before companions can delegate state reads.
- `PyErc20Token` (`py_erc20_token.rs`): `address`/`decimals`/`symbol`/`name` — **complete**.
- Python `Bot` (`src/degenbot/bot.py`, 608 lines) constructs `self._py_bot = PyBot()` at line 90 and **delegates nothing** — all state still in pure-Python pools/tokens via `PoolRegistry`/`TokenRegistry`/`ManagedPoolRegistry`. The companion migration is 0% done on the Python side.
- `UniswapArbEngine` (Rust) holds its own `Arc<Mutex<Bot>>`, registers V3/V4 via snapshot/backfill (`PyUniswapArbEngine.load_v3/v4_snapshot_from_py`, etc.) — a **separate `Bot` instance** from `PyBot`. Dual-state for engine-managed pools is the existing consistent baseline (closes via slice 10).

**Companion targets (migration weight).**
| Class | Lines | Family | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Erc20Token` | — | token | Simplest; `PyErc20Token` already complete. Price oracle + display stay Python. |
| `UniswapV2Pool` | 563 | V2 | 3-mixin (`V2PoolState`+`UniswapV2PoolCalc`+`PublisherMixin`+`PoolPickleMixin`+`AbstractLiquidityPool`); `__init__` takes `deployer_address`/`init_hash`/`factory`/`fee_token0`/`fee_token1` → maps onto `DexIdentity`; state in `StateCache[UniswapV2PoolState]`. |
| `UniswapV3Pool` | 1075 | V3 | `ConcentratedLiquidityStateManager[UniswapV3PoolState]`; tick data + sqrt/liquidity. Rust already owns V3 state. |
| `UniswapV4Pool` | 1169 | V4 | Like V3 + hook filtering + pool keys; registers via engine path, not `PyBot`. |
| `CurveStableswapPool` | 1140 | Curve | **Most Polars-like already**: `CurveDataProvider` seam (13 methods) + `DyCalculator` strategy seam (I/O-free). Uses `BoundedCache`, NOT in `PoolEntry` — "third family" (ADR-003 deferred). |
| `BalancerV2Pool` | 435 | Balancer | No state cache; `external_update` + `_state_lock`; `WeightedMath` functions; `PowVersion`. Not in `PoolEntry`. |
| `BalancerV2StablePool` | 759 | Balancer | `StableMath`; two invariant versions (V1/V2); `StaleRateResult`/`CacheAwareRateProvider`. |

**DEX subclasses to collapse (stance B).** `SushiswapV2Pool` (1 ClassVar), `PancakeswapV2Pool` (ClassVar + `FEE` + `RESERVES_STRUCT_TYPES`), `SwapbasedV2Pool` (1 ClassVar), `CamelotLiquidityPool` (`CamelotPoolCalc` stable branch via `_wire_camelot_calculations`/`_calc_tokens_out_fn`), `AerodromeV2Pool` (`FEE_DENOMINATOR` + custom `_decode_aerodrome_v2_sync` + stable branch). Per grilling: only Camelot/Aerodrome have genuine behavioral divergence (already mixin/decoder-shaped).

**Protocols/ABCs companions must satisfy.** `AbstractLiquidityPool` (`address`/`name`/`tokens`/`simulate_swap`), `AbstractErc20Token` (`address`/`symbol`/`name`/`decimals`); runtime-checkable `ConstantProductPool`/`ConcentratedLiquidityPool`/`StableswapPool`; `PoolBuilder`/`AsyncPoolBuilder` (`build`/`update` with `io` param); `BuilderContext` frozen dataclass.

**Registries/Bot session.** `PoolRegistry`, `TokenRegistry`, `ManagedPoolRegistry` (must hand out companions over `Py*`); `Bot._builders` (builder registry), Pool Type Registry (`(chain_id, factory) → class + identity`); `Bot.build_pool`/`build_erc20token`/`build_managed_pool` + type resolution (`type_resolution.py`).

When work on slices 3/4 lands, close `TODO-69cc2bea` as superseded by this master + those slices. (Its title still uses the old `PyPool` name — renamed to `PyLiquidityPool` by ADR-005 slice 2.)

**Adjacent open TODOs this migration interacts with:**

- `9235dd20` (open) "Lock granularity — Mutex held for entire solve_dirty" — overlaps slice 10's lock-semantics rework; coordinate.

---

## Slice 3 (Erc20Token purge) — DONE. Findings that reshape Slides 4-9:

- **~2× construction churn vs. surveyed.** Direct `Erc20Token(...)` sites: ~70 (surveyed ~40), across ~25 files incl. integration tests/conftests/fakes/optimizer tests. Resolved via `sed` construction-swap + a `make_erc20`/`make_ether_placeholder` test helper (`tests/helpers/erc20_factory.py`, idempotent via `get_token`-first because `Bot::register_token` asserts on dup). **Slice 4 (V2 pools) will be WORSE: V2 pools are constructed directly far more often than tokens.** Either budget heavy mechanical churn from the start OR introduce a transitional `LiquidityPool.from_state(...)`-style factory + converse approach before the pure purge. Re-examine the per-slice "small proof-of-concept" expectation for pool companions — they aren't small.
- **Pickle breakage is systemic and reaches the POOL tier.** Tokens hold non-picklable `Py*` handles → `Erc20Token.__getstate__` drops the handle (detached-snapshot unpickled tokens). **Every pool-family slice (4/8/9) will need the same `__getstate__`-drop-the-handle on the pool companion** (pools pickle via `PoolPickleMixin`; their own `PyLiquidityPool` handle is equally non-picklable). The detached-snapshot pattern is now the template — bake it into the slice design from the start rather than discovering it.
- **B-ii confirmed right call for calc.** Slice 3 didn't touch calc (tokens have none); but the pickle issue is exactly why "Rust owns state, Python keeps I/orchestration" must hold the line — don't let the handle leak into pickled graphs beyond the documented detach.
- **`chain_id` getter added to `PyErc20Token`** (Rust) — precedent: companion metadata getters that delegate to `TokenEntry`/state structs land on the `Py*` wrapper as the companion needs them. Expect the same read-getter additions on `PyLiquidityPool` (reserves/fee/factory/tokens) in Slice 4.

Slice 3 commit pending user review of the pickle-detach consequence + the blow-up count.

---

## Slice 15 added — `TODO-cddc72d1` "Retire pickle multiprocessing; land Rust-side parallel solve fan-out"

**Why:** Pickle exists only to feed `concurrent.futures`/`ProcessPoolExecutor` (verified zero in-repo consumers). Replacement is Rust-side `tokio::spawn`/`rayon` path-solve fan-out over the shared `Bot` (primitives already present). Scope: delete `PoolPickleMixin` + `pool_pickle.py` + `Erc20Token.__getstate__` (Slice 3's transient hack) + any per-pool `__getstate__` hacks slices 4-9 add + the pickle tests (audit each); land the Rust parallel solve fan-out; update the Curve `ProcessPoolExecutor` docstring.

**Sequencing:** the pickle-test/mixin removal is independent (can be pulled early, even now, to avoid the recurring `__getstate__`-hack churn across slices 4-9); the Rust fan-out pairs with Slice 10 (unified engine for a single shared `Bot`). **Bundled as one slice per the user ruling** ("remove the pickle tests as a slice of that effort") — unless the user later opts to split (15a removal / 15b fan-out) to keep slices 4-9 hack-free.

**Updated slice table (3-15):**

| # | Slice | TODO id |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Erc20Token companion *(done — carries a transient `__getstate__` until 15)* | TODO-2b633cf6 |
| 4 | V2 companion — state delegation | TODO-147dc6a6 |
| 5 | V2 companion — calc delegation | TODO-8d803585 |
| 6 | DexIdentity + DEX presets in Rust core | TODO-a42cd3d7 |

| 8 | V3 companion | TODO-bc71cd37 |
| 9 | V4 companion (library path) | TODO-9ac909c4 |
| 10 | UniswapEngine lock unification (closes 9356aaf7) | TODO-408eb2c1 |
| 11 | Curve family port | TODO-4324d069 |

| 13 | Crate split (degenbot-core / -python / umbrella) | TODO-41b7b22e |
