**Recommended order (revised):** 3 → 4 → 5 → (6 ∥ pre-7) → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10 → 11/12 → 13 → 14, with **15** :'s removal sub-step collapsible early alongside any of 4-9 (to shed the `__getstate__`-hack churn) and its Rust-fan-out sub-step after 10. Slices 4-9 each carry a transient per-class `__getstate__` hack (drop the non-picklable `Py*` handle) — Slice 15 retires that whole pattern + the pickle tests in one pass.

---

## Slice 4 DONE — `84f21384` (+ `7122f39e`, `585dbc8a`) "UniswapV2Pool companion over PyLiquidityPool"

The V2 companion pattern is proven end-to-end (the second companion after slice 3's `Erc20Token`). `UniswapV2Pool.__init__` takes a `PyLiquidityPool` handle; mutable state (reserves + reorg journal) reads/writes through it via an atomic `snapshot()`; immutable identity + calc stay Python (slice 5). **Two latent bugs fixed** along the way: (1) the V2 reorg journal's `restore_before_block` returned wrong values (the `*_before` at the target + the pre-newest on no-op) — corrected to landed-at semantics with a genesis delta + `*_after` fields; (2) `simulate_exact_input/output_swap(override_state=X)` built `final_state` from LIVE reserves while computing the delta from X — made consistent. 4 commits, ~75 construction conversions via a fresh-PyBot-per-call `make_v2_pool` helper, fork tests rewritten + anvil-verified. **Verified:** `cargo test` 467, clippy/rustfmt clean, ruff/ty/fmt on `src/` (387), 289 Python tests incl. anvil-verified fork discard/restore/override. Skipped the sole `concurrent.futures` test (slice-15-retired, pre-existing-broken).

**Updated slice table:** slice 4 status → **done**. Next actionable per the master's recommended order: **Slice 5** (V2 companion — calc delegation, `TODO-8d803585`) — moves V2 calc (`calculate_tokens_in/out_from_tokens_in/out`, `extract_fee`) to the Rust `PyLiquidityPool` (already has `calculate_tokens_out/in`; the companion would delegate). Then 6 (`DexIdentity` in Rust core), 7 (DEX subclass collapse).

---

## Slice 5 DONE — `b6bdeb16` "delegate V2 calc to PyLiquidityPool"

Calc delegation lands for the constant-product path: `UniswapV2PoolCalc.calculate_tokens_out_from_tokens_in` / `calculate_tokens_in_from_tokens_out` route to `self._py_pool.calculate_tokens_out/in(...)` on the NON-override path (Rust reads reserves + fee under one read guard — no Python state read beforehand, so a pump `sync_reserves` can't interleave between calc reads). Override path stays Python so `simulate_*` can hold one snapshot Python-side (slice-4's delta-consistency fix). Camelot/Aerodrome stable strategies remain pure Python (ADR-005 B-ii).

**TDD shape:** 9 new delegation-detection tests in `TestV2CalcDelegation` (`tests/uniswap/v2/test_v2_pool_io_free.py`) — `_DelegateSpy` wraps a `PyLiquidityPool` to record `calculate_tokens_out/in` calls (via `__getattr__` pass-through for state getters), so the tests assert "Rust was hit with the right `(zero_for_one, amount)`" rather than "result matches" (the parity tests already guarantee the math via `test_py_bot.py`). 5 delegation-detection tests red before implementation, 4 happy-path regressions pass.

**Two latent bugs surfaced + fixed:**
1. **Register-time fee-convention mismatch** (the big one). Slice-4's `make_v2_pool`, `V2PoolBuilder`, `CamelotBuilder` all registered `gamma_numerN = fee_tokenN.numerator` (fee semantics — 3 for 0.3% fee). But Rust's `IntHopState` (per its docs + parity tests) treats `gamma_numer` as the RETAINED POST-FEE fraction (`fee_denom - fee.numerator` — 997 for 0.3%). Slice-4 never invoked a Rust calc on a Python-built V2 pool (it routed everything through `simulate_*` which passes an override → Python calc). Slice-5's delegation routes direct no-override calls through Rust → exposes the mismatch: Python returned the correct on-chain `getAmountOut` (564_306_081_156_850_938 ≈ 0.56 WETH for 1000 USDC), Rust-as-registered returned 1_722_257_478_539_954 (~332× too small — exactly the 99.7% fee-as-loss factor). Fixed by registering the complement everywhere a fee Fraction is the source: new `_gamma_complement(fee) -> (fee.denominator - fee.numerator, fee.denominator)` helper in `make_v2_pool`; `fee_token.denominator - fee_token.numerator` in both builders. The `test_py_bot.py` parity tests already used the complement convention (they were the canonical reference).

2. **Slice-4 sentinel leftovers.** `'0xt0'`/`'0xt1'`/`'0xt2'`/`'0xtokenA'`/`'0xtokenB'`/`'0xtokenC'` short non-hex-flagged token sentinels in `tests/arbitrage/test_path/*.py` — slice-4 only caught the `'0xT0'` family (uppercase). `make_v2_pool`'s `register_v2_pool` parses the token address, failing on short sentinels with `ValueError: invalid string length`. Replaced with valid 40-hex sentinels (aaa/bbb/ccc ×40 and 111/222/333 ×40). 69 `test_path/` tests re-enabled.

**Verified green at commit:** `cargo fmt --check` + `clippy --lib --tests -D warnings` (Rust unchanged: 467 + 14 + 9 tests); `just fmt-check-python` (387 src/ files) + `just lint-python` (ruff + ty clean); 390 Python tests pass (367 slice-4 baseline + 23 engine + 9 new slice-5); 1 pre-existing-broken `test_base_2pool` requires `/node:8545` anvil infra (verified pre-existing at slice-4 commit). Anvil-verified under `anvil 1.7.1`: `test_create_camelot_v2_pool` (on-chain `getAmountOut` parity + builder-conversion of `FEE_DENOMINATOR`/`token0FeePercent`/`token1FeePercent`), `test_simulations_with_override` (override-reserves-consistent calc).

**Design realized:** V2 companion fully delegates (state via `snapshot()` + calc via `calculate_tokens_out/in` + sync_reserves/discard/restore via the handle) to Rust **except**: (a) the override path — `simulate_*` returns Python calc against the local snapshot (slice-4's design); (b) Camelot/Aerodrome stable strategy fns (ADR-005 B-ii). Aerodrome entirely untouched this slice (own state mixin — separate slice).

**Updated slice table:** slice 5 status → **done**. Next actionable per the master's recommended order: **Slice 6** (`DexIdentity` + DEX presets in Rust core, `TODO-a42cd3d7`) — the standalone-land Rust-core data layer (no Python consumer this slice; future consumers in slice 7). Then 7 (DEX subclass collapse).

---

## Slice 6 DONE — `31ba43bc` "DexIdentity + DEX presets in Rust core (ADR-005 slice 6)"

The standalone-Rust `DexIdentity` registry + 8 `pub const` DEX presets land in the pure-Rust core (zero pyo3 — verified). This is the foundational "standalone constraint" data layer: a future standalone Rust consumer can `cargo add degenbot-core` and construct a Sushiswap V2 pool without any Python import. Exposed via a Python seam (`#[pyfunction] dex_identity(variant)` + frozen `#[pyclass] PyDexIdentity` view) for slice 7's first consumer.

**TDD shape:** 14 Rust unit tests in `dex_identity.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` mod + 9 Python seam tests in `test_py_bot.py::TestDexIdentityPresets`. Red phase = presets set to `Address::ZERO`/`B256::ZERO`/`(0,0)` placeholders → 7 preset-value unit tests fail with `left == ZERO` assertions. Green = fill in the verified Python ClassVar values cross-checked against `src/degenbot/{uniswap,sushiswap,pancakeswap,swapbased,camelot,aerodrome}/__init__.py` `v2_deployments`/`_factory_address` + the FEE/FEE_DENOMINATOR/init-hash ClassVars. The 9 Python tests mirror the same assertions through the FFI seam.

**Design realized:**
- `DexIdentity` struct mirrors the `V2PoolState` field types exactly (`Address`, `(u64,u64)` fees) so slice 7 can feed `register_v2_pool(gamma_numerN=identity.fee_tokenN.0, fee_denomN=identity.fee_tokenN.1, factory=identity.factory, ...)` directly — no convention translation at the consumption point.
- `fee_tokenN: (u64, u64)` = `(gamma_numer, fee_denom)` — the RETAINED post-fee fraction (slice-5 convention). PancakeSwap's `Fraction(25, 10000)` → preset `(9975, 10_000)`. The module doc + field doc + the tests bake this in explicitly to guard against re-introducing the slice-5 bug.
- Added `reserves_abi: ReservesAbi` + `init_hash: B256` fields beyond the literal TODO struct spec — ADR-005 names both ("init hash" + "ABI struct shapes"); the acceptance test checks Pancake's `RESERVES_STRUCT_TYPES`. `init_hash` is NEW data (`V2PoolState` doesn't store it per ADR-005: "identity is NOT a field on V2PoolState").
- Python seam: `#[pyclass(frozen, skip_from_py_object)] #[derive(Clone)] PyDexIdentity` — a COPY view (hex-string addresses, int-tuple fees) cached in a `OnceLock<HashMap>`. `skip_from_py_object` opts out of the deprecated auto-`FromPyObject` that deriving `Clone` on a pyclass triggers. `#[pyfunction] dex_identity(variant)` is case-insensitive kebab lookup, returns `None` for unrecognized (no `PanicException`).
- Camelot stable + Aerodrome stable presets carry `gamma_numer=0` (no compile-time default — fees are per-pool on-chain) with the documented denominator. Aerodrome `init_hash` is `B256::ZERO` (Python source says "different address generation"; address derivation for Aerodrome is a separate path, deferred to a future slice).

**Acceptance (all met at commit):** cargo green (fmt + `clippy --lib --tests -D warnings` + **481 tests** = 467 + 14 new); `rg 'use pyo3' rust/src/bot_core/dex_identity.rs` empty (core pyo3-free); `pyfunction` callable from Python returning the preset (9 seam tests); preset unit tests match Python ClassVars (UNISWAP_V2_MAINNET_POOL_INIT_HASH; Pancake `Fraction(25,10000)` + `RESERVES_STRUCT_TYPES`; Aerodrome `FEE_DENOMINATOR=10000`; `CAMELOT_ARBITRUM_POOL_INIT_HASH`). Inert addition — zero regressions (344 Python tests across the V2/companion pyramid pass).

**Process note:** the initial `git commit` missed the 2 new files (`git add -u` stages only modified-tracked files, not new untracked ones). Caught via the "4 files changed" summary vs the 6 expected; amended to include them (`31ba43bc` final = 6 files, +859). The committed state is self-contained green (rebuilt + re-ran the 14+9 tests from the committed tree). Lesson for future slices: when adding new files, `git add rust/src/...` explicitly, not just `git add -u`.

**Updated slice table:** slice 6 status → **done**. Next actionable per the master's recommended order: **Slice 7** (`DEX subclass collapse` stance B, `TODO-38f34cf3`) — the first consumer of these presets. Drops `SushiswapV2Pool`/`PancakeswapV2Pool`/`SwapbasedV2Pool` subclasses (which only carry a `variant` ClassVar + `FEE`/`RESERVES_STRUCT_TYPES`) in favor of `UniswapV2Pool` constructed with a `DexIdentity` preset. Camelot/Aerodrome keep their own calc mixins (genuine behavioral divergence — ADR-005 B-ii). Deps satisfied: slice 4 (V2 companion) + slice 5 (calc delegation) + slice 6 (DexIdentity) all done.

data.title: Consolidate bot startup to one canonical path
Write context-map maintenance contract
data.body:
## Goal
- Write a single-source-of-truth maintenance contract for the context-map corpus (`CONTEXT-MAP.md` + module `CONTEXT.md` files + `rust/CONTEXT.md`) so future ADR-driven edits have explicit rules and stop re-rotting the vocabulary files.
- Cross-link it from `AGENTS.md`'s "Domain docs" agent-skill section so agents discover it.

## Context — why this exists
A prior review found that almost all drift in the context maps concentrates wherever a refactor's history was written into the vocabulary file instead of its ADR. The corpus's own root-level `## Instructions` section has rules (term belongs to one module, ambiguity goes where the ambiguity lives, keep the map in sync) but no rule on *what belongs in a definition vs. what belongs in an ADR*, and no status-tag convention. This task fills that gap so the structural-rewrite and validation tasks can cite a single contract.

`AGENTS.md` already says "context maps" live as a multi-context system under `docs/agents/` (see the Domain docs bullet referencing `docs/agents/domain.md`). Add the new doc next to it.

## Acceptance Criteria
Create `docs/agents/context-map-maintenance.md` (≤ ~50 lines) stating:
1. A context-map entry = what the term means now + aliases-to-avoid + (optional) ≤1 footgun note. It is NOT a changelog, design diary, or status report.
2. When an ADR lands, the only permitted context-map edit is "term now means X; link to ADR-N." Implementation history, "formerly", "revised by", and "status: complete" narratives go in the ADR — never in the vocabulary file.
3. Status vocabulary = `{Live | Removed}`, written as a trailing parenthetical tag (e.g. `**Foo** (Removed): ...`). No prose status paragraphs. Removed terms are grouped in a `## Removed terms` block per file, one line each, naming the ADR/plan that removed them.
4. The `{Foo}` brace-dialect is banned. Use real markdown links (`[Term](#anchor)` or relative file paths) or plain `**Term**`.
5. Definitions capped at ~4 sentences / ~80 words. "Why" narratives belong in ADRs.
6. The root `CONTEXT-MAP.md` Cross-module relationships section holds ONLY cross-module seams — a bullet belongs there only if it names ≥2 module terms. Single-module relationships stay in that module's `CONTEXT.md`.
7. Modules at target shape (do not "tidy"): `erc20/`, `listener/`, `curve/`, `balancer/`, `aave/`, `uniswap/`, `types/`, `builders/`. (List is informational; these need no changes.)

Add to `AGENTS.md`'s "Domain docs" agent-skill line a pointer: `See docs/agents/context-map-maintenance.md for the vocabulary-file rules (status tags, brace-dialect ban, ADR-not-vocabulary for history).`

## Validation Gates
- `test -f docs/agents/context-map-maintenance.md` → exists
- `rg -n "context-map-maintenance" AGENTS.md` → the pointer line present
- `wc -l docs/agents/context-map-maintenance.md` → ≤ ~55
- `rg -n "Live \| Removed|brace-dialect|game|ADR-not-vocabulary|≥2 module terms" docs/agents/context-map-maintenance.md` → the key rules present

data.title: Add lint-context-maps validation target + CI wiring
data.body:
## Goal
- Add a `just lint-context-maps` target (and wire it into `just lint`) that enforces the context-map maintenance contract from the sibling "Write maintenance contract" task, so drift is caught by CI rather than re-accumulating.
- The target must be cheap (no new heavy deps), grep-based, and fail loud.

## Context — the contract being enforced
The maintenance contract (`docs/agents/context-map-maintenance.md`, written by a sibling task) bans (a) the `{Foo}` brace-dialect, (b) status-prose markers (`Status: complete`, `Revised by ADR-`, `Prior to ADR-`), and (c) broken relative links. This task makes those rules executable. The structural-rewrite task removes the existing violations; this task guards against regressions.

The corpus to scan: `CONTEXT-MAP.md`, `rust/CONTEXT.md`, `src/degenbot/*/CONTEXT.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
Add to `justfile` (alongside the existing `lint-rust`/lint-python targets) a `lint-context-maps` recipe that:
1. Asserts no `{Foo}` brace-dialect in any CONTEXT file: `rg -n "\{[A-Z][^}]+\}" CONTEXT-MAP.md rust/CONTEXT.md src/degenbot/*/CONTEXT.md` → must be empty (exit non-zero on match).
2. Asserts no status-prose markers: `rg -n "Status: complete|Implementation status|Revised by ADR-|Prior to ADR-" rust/CONTEXT.md CONTEXT-MAP.md` → must be empty.
3. Asserts no references to the deleted connection module: `rg -n "src/degenbot/connection/CONTEXT" CONTEXT-MAP.md` and `rg -ni "connection manager" CONTEXT-MAP.md src/degenbot/provider/CONTEXT.md` → must be empty.
4. Asserts every relative-link target in CONTEXT files resolves (a small script or `markdown-link-check` if already available; if adding a dep is too heavy, a grep+`test -f` loop over `(](...CONTEXT.md)` and `(](rust/...)` style links is acceptable — keep it dependency-free).
5. Wires `lint-context-maps` into the existing `lint` recipe so `just lint` runs it.

Prefer a `rg`-based implementation that does not pull new packages. If a broken-link check truly needs `markdown-link-check`, gate it behind a `[lint-docs]` optional extra instead of adding a hard dep — but the simpler grep approach is preferred.

## Validation Gates
- `just lint-context-maps` runs and exits 0 (because the structural-rewrite + drift tasks have already removed all violations) — verify on a clean checkout of this branch's tasks
- `just lint` still runs `lint-context-maps` (grep the justfile to confirm the recipe is listed)
- Temporarily introduce a `{Test}` brace in any CONTEXT file → `just lint-context-maps` exits non-zero (proves the check actually fires)
- `just test-rust` and `just test-python` still pass (no code changed; sanity)

## Goal

## Context — the rules every definition must follow
A context-map definition = **what the term means now** + aliases-to-avoid + (optional) ≤1 footgun note. It is NOT a changelog. Status, when needed, is a trailing tag like `**Foo** (Removed):` — never a prose "Status: complete" paragraph. "Why" narratives belong in ADRs (`docs/adr/`), not in vocabulary entries. Definitions capped at ~4 sentences / ~80 words.

Verified code facts to cite (these contradict the current doc text — fix the doc to match the code):
- `Bot::new` signature is `pub fn new(chain_id: u64) -> Self` at `rust/src/bot_core/mod.rs:1968` — NO `rpc_url` argument (the doc currently claims `Bot::new(chain_id, rpc_url)`).
- `with_core` takes `Arc<parking_lot::RwLock<BotState>>` at `rust/src/bot_core/mod.rs:1985` (NOT `Bot`; the doc says "both PyBot and UniswapEngine adopt a clone (with_core/from_core)").
- `EventSink` IS a real trait: `rust/src/bot_core/engine.rs:4,27`. `PoolStateSubscriber` IS a real trait: `rust/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs:40`. The `Bot` doc field `Vec<Box<dyn EventSink>>` appears at `rust/src/bot_core/mod.rs:1923`. `ReorgCoordinator` at `rust/src/bot_core/reorg_coordinator.rs:112`; `BlockPump` at `rust/src/bot_core/block_pump.rs:107`; `LogDispatcher` at `rust/src/bot_core/log_dispatcher.rs`. So the `EventSink` entry's `(ADR-006, concept + coalesced-timing decided; exact change-set shape deferred)` intro is FLAT WRONG — this is shipped, not deferred.
- `TickMap` trait IS implemented: `rust/src/bot_core/tick_map.rs:41`, `impl TickMap for V3PoolState` at line 74. So "ADR-004 adds a TickMap trait" must be present-tense ("ADR-004's `TickMap` trait (`rust/src/bot_core/tick_map.rs:41`) narrows...").

## Acceptance Criteria — a checklist, one item per ballooned term
Rewrite these term definitions to present tense, ≤~80 words each (file:line of the current text):
1. `**Bot**` (line 47): drop `(formerly BotCore)`, `Bot::new(chain_id, rpc_url)` → `Bot::new(chain_id)`, drop "with_core/from_core" (replace with "`with_core` takes `Arc<RwLock<BotState>>`"), delete the entire "Prior to ADR-006 (status pre-revision)" paragraph (line 49) — ADR-006 owns that history.

Replace with ≤4 sentences naming both the `EventSink` trait and `PoolStateSubscriber` trait (both at the file:lines above) and the current single impl (`UniswapArbEngine`). Delete the `SolvePolicy` deferral aside entirely.
4. `**Reorg Journal**` (line 91): keep the one-paragraph present-tense definition (delta mechanism, `restore_before_block`, depth default 32, `Bot::with_journal_depth`). Delete "Implementation status (Plan 100, complete)" and the entire "Revised by ADR-006:" paragraph. Delete the "previously-latent V3 partial-priors bug ... is fixed" sentence — that fix narrative, if worth keeping, belongs in ADR-003; out of scope here (just delete from this file).
5. `**Slot0 Head / Tick Bookkeeping Map**` (line 94): trim to ≤4 sentences: the two-part conceptual split + the `TickMap` trait (citing `rust/src/bot_core/tick_map.rs:41`). Delete the "TODO-6177b602 survey (148 V3 + 184 V4 field accesses → 22 function-level surfaces)..." paragraph and the "rejected by survey evidence" / "hold reason recorded previously" archaeology — that belongs in ADR-004.

data.body:
## Goal

## Acceptance Criteria
Delete these single-module bullets from `CONTEXT-MAP.md` (verified line numbers):
- Balancer cluster (lines ~52–66): `BalancerV2StablePool` MetaStable/Composable handling, `CacheAwareRateProvider`/exact-0-wei, invariant V1/V2 (2 bullets), `BROKEN_BALANCER_V2_POOLS`, `BalancerBuilder`, `BalancerBuilderBase`, `BalancerPairView`, `BalancerV2SwapAmounts`, Balancer Pool→Hop conversion, `external_update` lock pattern. **pi id:** `TODO-071d4791`

**tags:** `deferred`, `mev-bot`, `encoding`, `permutation-runner`

---

Follow-up session: investigate why exotic permutations (e.g. V4-V3-V4, V4-V3-V2) show high simulation revert rates / wrong hop counts in the permutation runner logs.

Sources:
- `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py` dispatch & path-building logic
- `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py` command-stream encoders
- `logs/permutation_results.tsv` and per-permutation `.log` files under `logs/`

Likely starting points:
1. Confirm whether `find_paths_async` with `pool_type_per_depth` returns shorter paths when a full N-hop path cannot be closed, leading to unexpected 2-hop results in 3-hop filters.
2. Audit encoders for the red/Partial rows in `logs/permutation_results.tsv` for balance/order-of-operations bugs (e.g. `ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance`).
3. Add per-revert taxonomy logging so each failed simulation is classified by root cause rather than a single bucket.

Related to the Rust solver work sessions currently in progress.

## Progress (2026-06-20)

### (3) Per-revert taxonomy logging — DONE
`[sim]` summary previously lumped every failed simulation into one opaque
`N failed` count. Added a pure, unit-tested classifier and wired it into the
dispatcher so the summary now breaks failures down by root cause, e.g.
`[sim] 12 candidates: 0 ok ..., 12 failed — by reason: CurrencyNotSettled=9 ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance=3`.

- `examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`: new `_classify_revert(revert_data) -> str`
  (canonical short label: `CurrencyNotSettled`, `InsufficientProfit`, decoded
  `Error(string)` message, `Panic(0x..)`, `numeric-revert`, `unknown:0xsel`,
  `empty`), `_format_failure_breakdown(dict) -> str`, and the selector maps
  `_V4_REVERT_SELECTORS` / `_EXECUTOR_REVERT_SELECTORS` as canonical data.
- `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`: `_fail_buckets` tally + `_tally_fail`
  at every simulate_one failure branch (revert / no-profit / rpc-failed /
  balance-decode / int128-overflow); breakdown appended to the `[sim]` line.
  Existing verbose `[sim-fail]` per-fail decode untouched.
- Regression tests: `tests/arbitrage/test_revert_taxonomy.py` (11 cases).

### (1) Shorter-path finding — CONFIRMED
`logs/perm-V4-V3-V4.log` shows `[dispatch] simulating 2/2 candidates: V4-V3=2`
under the `V4-V3-V4` 3-hop filter — `find_paths_async` with `pool_type_per_depth`
emits closed 2-hop `V4-V3` cycles (e.g. WETH→USDC via V4, USDC→WETH via V3)
because the DFS prunes edges by depth but still closes a cycle in 2 hops when
the pair inverts. The 2-hop path is a genuine arb; the dispatch label `V4-V3`
correctly reflects actual hops, not a bug in labeling. Worth verifying whether
the permutation harness's `PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER` should additionally constrain
path *length* (not just per-depth type) if pure-3-hop coverage is desired.

### (2) Encoder audit — V3-V4-V3 `CurrencyNotSettled` ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSED
Row #17 (V3-V4-V3, 50%) reverts 100% on its revert branch with
`CurrencyNotSettled()` (selector `0x5212cba1`). Root cause identified by
cross-referencing V4-core `PoolManager.sync`/`settle` semantics
(`contract_reference/uniswap/V4/PoolManager.sol`) with the executor's V3
callback (`~/code/executor/contracts/cmd_executor.vy:uniswapV3SwapCallback`)
and the encoder `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` (`examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`):

- V4 `sync(currency)` only *baselines* `balanceOfSelf`; `settle()` then credits
  `paid = balanceNow − baseline` as a +delta. So a deposit must land *between*
  a sync and a settle to be captured.
- A V3 pool transfers its **output** to the recipient only **after** its swap
  callback returns. The executor runs the V3 callback's forward_data
  synchronously (`cmd_executor.vy:uniswapV3SwapCallback`).
- In `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` the nesting is `V3c →(c_fwd) V3a →(a_fwd) ERC20_TRANSFER + V4_UNLOCK(v4_inner)`.
  The V4 swap (consuming `forward_a`) runs *inside V3a's callback*, but V3a
  delivers `forward_a` to PM only *after* that callback returns. At unlock time
  `forward_a` is absent; the static `out_a` V4_SWAP_COMPACT leaves a `−out_a`
  forward_a delta; PM.unlock's final nonzero-delta check fires
  `CurrencyNotSettled`.

This is a **nesting-order bug**, not a stale-amount bug — so the
V2-V2-V4-style "swap COMPACT→DYNAMIC + settle_all" patch alone is insufficient.
Correct fix requires re-nesting so V3a runs *inside* the V4-unlock inner
(after `SYNC(forward_a)`; before `SETTLE; V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC; V4_TAKE_DELTA(forward_b→V3c); SETTLE_ALL`), so the forward_a deposit lands between
sync and settle. See follow-up ergo task (Spin-out below) — NOT landed here
because the multi-callback restructure needs live / Foundry executor-test
validation, which this session could not perform.

data.title: Fix _3hop_v3_v4_v3 nesting order (CurrencyNotSettled root cause)
data.body:
# Fix `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` nesting order (CurrencyNotSettled root cause)

**tags:** `mev-bot`, `encoding`, `permutation-runner`

Spun out of J5HSR7 (diagnosis complete; fix NOT landed because it needs live /
Foundry executor-test validation this session could not run).

## Root cause (verified against contract reference)

Row #17 (V3-V4-V3, 50% in `logs/permutation_results.tsv`) reverts 100% on its
revert branch with `CurrencyNotSettled()` (selector `0x5212cba1`).

In `_3hop_v3_v4_v3` (`examples/eth_backrun_helpers.py`) the nesting is
`V3c →(c_fwd) V3a →(a_fwd) ERC20_TRANSFER + V4_UNLOCK(v4_inner)`. The V4 swap
(consuming `forward_a`) runs *inside V3a's callback*, but:

- V4 `sync(currency)` only baselines `balanceOfSelf`; `settle()` credits
  `paid = balanceNow − baseline` (see `contract_reference/uniswap/V4/PoolManager.sol:sync/_settle`).
- A V3 pool transfers its output to the recipient only **after** its swap
  callback returns (`~/code/executor/contracts/cmd_executor.vy:uniswapV3SwapCallback`
  runs forward_data synchronously during the callback).

So at V4-unlock time `forward_a` is absent; the static `out_a`
`V4_SWAP_COMPACT` leaves a `−out_a` forward_a delta; `PM.unlock`'s final
nonzero-delta check fires `CurrencyNotSettled`.

This is a **nesting-order** bug, so the V2-V2-V4-style "COMPACT→DYNAMIC +
settle_all" patch alone is insufficient.

## Fix

Re-nest so V3a runs **inside** the V4-unlock inner, between `SYNC(forward_a)`
and `SETTLE`, so the forward_a deposit lands between sync and settle:

- Top: `V3c_swap(recipient=executor, forward_data=c_fwd)`
- `c_fwd = V4_UNLOCK(v4_inner)` (move V4 unlock up from V3a's callback into V3c's)
- `v4_inner`:
  1. `V4_SYNC(forward_a)`            — baseline PM forward_a balance (0)
  2. `V3a_swap(recipient=PM, forward_data=ERC20_TRANSFER(WETH→V3a pool))` — pays
     V3a input; V3a returns → delivers forward_a to PM (deposit lands)
  3. `V4_SETTLE`                     — credits +X forward_a delta
  4. `V4_SWAP_DYNAMIC`               — consumes +X forward_a → +Y forward_b
  5. `V4_TAKE_DELTA(forward_b → V3c)` — routes full forward_b output to V3c pool
  6. `V4_SETTLE_ALL`                — settle WETH/native residual
- V3c callback returns → V3c sends WETH to executor.

Consider also making the outermost V3c `V3_SWAP_DELTA` (reads forward_b delta
from PM exttload) so the V3c input matches the actual V4 output exactly,
avoiding residual dust / `transfer amount exceeds balance` when actual ≠ `out_b`.

## Validation gate (required before close)

- Add a structural regression test in `tests/arbitrage/test_eth_backrun_helpers.py`
  pinning the new ordering (mirror the V2-V2-V4 test: assert V3a is *inside* the
  V4-unlock inner, swap is DYNAMIC, output is TAKE_DELTA, ends with SETTLE_ALL;
  assert V4_UNLOCK is NOT nested inside V3a's forward_data).
- Validate against live permutation runner (`PATH_PERMUTATION_FILTER={"V3-V4-V3"}`,
  15-min observation) — the `[sim] ... by reason:` breakdown from J5HSR7's
  taxonomy should show `CurrencyNotSettled` dropping to ~0 for V3-V4-V3.
- If a Foundry harness for `~/code/executor` 3-hop V3-V4-V3 is feasible, add an
  on-chain test there (more authoritative than the structural test).

## Related

- J5HSR7 (diagnosis + taxonomy logging — done)
- V2-V2-V4 precedent: commit `2e505536` (structural-test-only encoder fix)

data.title: ADR-007: settle B2 (PyPool-wrapping) + Rust unregister seam design
data.body:
## Goal
- Record the B1/B2/B3 decision (B2 settled) + the register/unregister seam design as ADR-007, closing the "decision this session must make" branch of IESD3L.

## Context
IESD3L's task body framed the construction-shape decision (what `Bot.build_pool` returns) as open. It isn't: ADR-005 slice 4 already landed B2 — every builder calls `_py_bot.register_v2/v3/v4_pool(...)` then `get_pool(pool_id)` and wraps the `PyLiquidityPool` handle in a Python companion (`LiquidityPool`, `UniswapV3Pool`, `UniswapV4Pool`), mirroring `Erc20Token`-wraps-`PyToken`. Evidence: `src/degenbot/builders/v2_pool_builder.py:146-165`, `engine_registry.py:148-151` ("ALREADY registered there by `bot.build_pool`… Re-registering via `engine.register_v2_pool` would panic"). Real library callers (`uniswap/trackers.py`, `curve/trackers.py`, `examples/eth_backrun_*.py`) consume `AbstractLiquidityPool` — B1 (raw `PyPool`) would break them, B3 (delete `PoolRegistry`) is a larger-blast-radius cleanup not required for correctness.

The actual open gap is Rust-side: `BotState` has `register_v2/v3/v4_pool` that `panic!` on duplicate address (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/mod.rs:285`, `:348`) but **no `unregister`**. So `PoolRegistry.remove` (`src/degenbot/registry/pool.py:156`) deletes the Python wrapper only; re-`build_pool` re-calls `register_v2_pool` and panics. This is what `test_uniswap_trackers.py::test_pool_remove_and_recreate` hits (`pyo3_runtime.PanicException: pool already registered`).

ADR-007 records the two decisions IESD3L still needs:
1. **B2 is settled** (cite ADR-005 slice 4 as the implementing decision). Do not re-open B1/B3 — the option matrix in the IESD3L body is now historical context.
2. **Duplicate-registration stays refusal-on-panic** (not idempotent-return-existing): `engine_registry`'s `_v2_keys`/`_v3_keys`/`_v4_keys` lean on the panic-as-invariant to detect double-registration; making register idempotent would silently mask divergent state. Removal is explicit and paired: `PoolRegistry.add` is preceded by PyBot register in the builders; `PoolRegistry.remove`/`reset` must be followed by PyBot unregister — symmetric seam.
3. **Unregister design**: address-keyed for V2/V3, `(pool_manager_address, pool_id)`-keyed for V4 (one PoolManager hosts many pool_ids — address alone is ambiguous). The Rust method signature mirrors Python's `PoolRegistry.remove(chain_id, pool_address, pool_id=None)`:
   - `BotState::unregister_pool(address: Address, pool_id: Option<PoolId>) -> bool`
   - V2/V3 path: resolves `pool_addresses[address]` → `pool_id`, deletes `pools[pool_id]` + `pool_addresses[address]`.
   - V4 path: resolves `v4_pool_ids[(pool_manager, pool_id)]` (the `address` arg IS the pool_manager_address for V4), deletes `pools[pool_id]` + `v4_pool_ids` entry + discards matching `v4_buffer` events (otherwise re-register would replay stale buffered ModifyLiquidity).
   - V3 path also discards matching `v3_buffer` events for that address (symmetric reason).
   - Journal is dropped with the `PoolEntry`. Reorg restore for a removed pool is a no-op target (the journal no longer exists).
   - Returns `true` if a pool was present + removed, `false` if not-found (Postel's law; Python `remove` returns None and is silent on miss today — keep that Python-side behavior, the bool is for testability + future engine-key cleanup).
   - **PyO3 method**: `PyBot::unregister_pool(address: &str, pool_id: Option<Vec<u8>>) -> PyResult<bool>` (None → V2/V3 path, `Some(bytes)` → V4 path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New file `docs/adr/ADR-007-pool-unregister-seam.md` with Status: accepted.
- States (1) B2 settled (cite ADR-005 slice 4), (2) duplicate-registration refusal-on-panic rationale, (3) the unregister signature/disposal rules above, (4) the symmetric Python seam (`PoolRegistry.add`/`remove`/`reset` + `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove` propagate to `PyBot`).
- Notes the engine-key cleanup as a known gap (out of scope here): `EngineRegistry._v2_keys`/`_v3_keys`/`_v4_keys` cache address→pool_id but `engine_registry.py` has no `unregister_pool` today — the engine does not exercise remove/recreate in any current test. Recorded for a future cleanup, not blockers.
- Cross-link from ADR-003 ("Out of scope for ADR-003, in scope here" → resolves to ADR-007).

## Validation Gates
- `just lint` clean.
- ADR renders in the docs tree; references resolve.

data.title: Rust: BotState::unregister_pool + PyBot::unregister_pool with buffer/journal disposal
data.body:
## Goal
- Add `BotState::unregister_pool` + `PyBot::unregister_pool` (PyO3) so removal propagates to Rust-owned state. Implements the design recorded in ADR-007 (task 223IU3).

## Context
- `BotState` (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/mod.rs`) holds pools in three maps: `pools: HashMap<u64, PoolEntry>`, `pool_addresses: HashMap<Address, u64>` (V2/V3), `v4_pool_ids: HashMap<(Address, PoolId), u64>` (V4). Plus `next_pool_id` (not reused — removed IDs are retired to avoid stale-handle aliasing) and the `v3_buffer`/`v4_buffer` `LiquidityEventBuffer`s holding events for unregistered pools.
- `register_v2/v3/v4_pool` `panic!` on duplicate address; that behavior stays.
- ADR-005: reorg journals (`V2BlockDelta`, V3/V4 equivalents) live on `PoolEntry`. Removed entry = journal dropped with it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `BotState::unregister_pool(&mut self, address: Address, pool_id: Option<PoolId>) -> bool`:
  - V2/V3 path (`pool_id` is None): if `pool_addresses` has `address`, remove from both `pools` and `pool_addresses`. If V3, also drain matching `v3_buffer` entries for that address (`v3_buffer.discard_for(&address)` or equivalent — check the `LiquidityEventBuffer` API; if no such method exists, add one symmetric with the existing discard helpers). Return `true` if removed, `false` if not found.
  - V4 path (`pool_id` is Some): the `address` arg is the PoolManager address. If `v4_pool_ids` has `(address, pool_id)`, remove from `pools`, `v4_pool_ids`, and drain `v4_buffer` for that key. Return `true`/`false`.
  - Does **not** reuse `next_pool_id` — retired IDs stay retired (avoids stale `PyLiquidityPool` handles aliasing to a different pool on recreate).
  - Calling `unregister_pool` on an unknown address/pool_id is a silent no-op returning `false` (not a panic — matches Python `PoolRegistry.remove`'s silent-on-miss behavior).
- `PyBot::unregister_pool(&self, address: &str, pool_id: Option<Vec<u8>>) -> PyResult<bool>` — parses address, converts `pool_id` bytes → `degenbot_decoders::v4_swap_decoder::PoolId` (or None), delegates to `BotState`. Mirrors the `register_v2_pool`/`register_v4_pool` PyO3 signature style (`#[pyo3(signature = (address, pool_id=None))]`).
- Unit tests in `bot_core/mod.rs` test module:
  - V2: register → unregister → re-register succeeds (no panic), pool_id is a fresh id (≠ first), `unregister_pool` on unknown returns `false`.
  - V3: same + buffered Mint/Burn events for the address are gone after unregister (verified by re-register not replaying them — or by direct buffer-empty assertion, whichever the test seam makes easiest).
  - V4: register → unregister by `(pool_manager, pool_id)` → re-register succeeds; buffered ModifyLiquidity discarded.
  - `unregister_pool` on never-registered address returns `false`, no mutation.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` green (new tests included).
- `just lint-rust` clean (no new clippy drift).
- `just fmt-check` clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` OK (PyBot lives in root `rust/src/`, not a core crate).

data.title: Python: wire PoolRegistry/ManagedPoolRegistry.remove+reset → PyBot.unregister_pool
data.body:
## Goal
- Wire Python `PoolRegistry.remove`/`reset` + `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove` → `PyBot.unregister_pool` so the Python↔Rust state seam stays symmetric with the builder's `add` direction. Unblocks `test_uniswap_trackers.py::test_pool_remove_and_recreate`.

## Context
- `PoolRegistry` (`src/degenbot/registry/pool.py`) has no reference to `PyBot` today — it's a pure address→pool store. The bot owns both: `bot.pools = PoolRegistry()` + `bot._py_bot = PyBot()` (`src/degenbot/bot.py:128-133`). The register direction already flows PyBot→PoolRegistry via the builders (`v2_pool_builder.py:146` registers in PyBot, then `_register_pool` adds to PoolRegistry at `:184`).
- The unregister direction has no seam: `PoolRegistry.remove` (`registry/pool.py:156`) deletes only the Python wrapper; `bot._py_bot` retains the entry; re-`build_pool` → `_py_bot.register_v2_pool` → `panic: pool already registered`.
- `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove` (`registry/pool.py:63`) is the V4 equivalent — keyed by `(chain_id, pool_manager_address, pool_id)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PoolRegistry.remove(chain_id, pool_address, pool_id=None)`:
  - V2/V3 path (no `pool_id`): before/after removing from the Python store, call `bot._py_bot.unregister_pool(address=pool_address, pool_id=None)`. If `PoolRegistry` has no `py_bot` reference today, add one (constructor arg `py_bot: PyBot | None = None`, default None for back-compat with tests that construct `PoolRegistry()` standalone — when `py_bot is None`, skip the Rust call, preserving current behavior). Wire `bot.py` to pass `py_bot=self._py_bot`.
  - V4 path (`pool_id` is bytes): delegate to `bot._py_bot.unregister_pool(address=pool_address, pool_id=pool_id)`. The `address` arg is the PoolManager address per ADR-007.
- `PoolRegistry._reset()` / `reset()`: iterate registered addresses and call `unregister_pool` for each before clearing. If `py_bot is None`, just clear.
- `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove`: same propagation by `(pool_manager_address, pool_id)`.
- `Bot.__init__` (`bot.py:133`): `self.pools = PoolRegistry(py_bot=self._py_bot)`.
- `AsyncBuilderContext` + sync `BuilderContext`: they construct their own `PoolRegistry`? Check (`src/degenbot/builders/context.py`, `async_context.py`) — if they receive `pools=` from `Bot` (they do — `bot.py:150` passes `pools=self.pools`), no change needed; the shared registry carries the `py_bot` reference.
- `test_uniswap_trackers.py::test_pool_remove_and_recreate` passes: `bot.pools.remove(...)` no longer leaves stale Rust state; the third `get_pool_from_tokens` build succeeds.

## Acceptance Criteria (helper-fix verification)
- The 3 currently-failing Python tests (`test_pool_remove_and_recreate`, the two `TestAsyncV2BuilderUpdateBehavior` tests from the prior slice) all pass. The async builder tests were already fixed in commit `283bfe62` (test-helper-only); confirm no regression.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-python` (or `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/uniswap/test_uniswap_trackers.py::test_pool_remove_and_recreate tests/builders/test_builder_update_staticmethod.py -q`) green.
- `just test-rust-python` green (PyO3 seam end-to-end).
- `just lint` clean (Python ruff + mypy on touched files).

data.title: Docs: sync unregister seam to layered docs + cross-link ADR-007
data.body:
## Goal
- Sync the layered docs (`rust/CONTEXT.md`, `rust/AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT-MAP.md`) so the unregister seam is discoverable, and cross-link ADR-007 from ADR-003's "in scope here" branch.

## Context
- Layered docs: `CONTEXT-MAP.md` (ubiquitous-language index) → per-module `CONTEXT.md` → `rust/AGENTS.md` (operational) → ADRs (`docs/adr/`). Mirror the doc-sync pattern used in Plans 104/105 for the decoders/uniswap crate extractions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `rust/CONTEXT.md`: add (or annotate if existing) `BotState::unregister_pool` to the BotCore terms, noting the V2/V3-address vs V4-(pool_manager,pool_id) keying and the silent-miss `false` return contract.
- `rust/AGENTS.md`: one-line note in the PyBot surface table that `register_*` panic-on-duplicate + the paired `unregister_pool` is the symmetric seam; warn that `next_pool_id` is not reused (retired IDs stay retired).
- `CONTEXT-MAP.md`: if it lists Rust-owned state operations, mention `unregister_pool`.
- `docs/adr/ADR-003-botcore-state-layer.md`: in the "Out of scope for ADR-003, in scope here" section, add a pointer line: "Resolved by ADR-007 (pool unregister seam + B2 settlement)."
- `docs/adr/ADR-007-*` cross-links back to ADR-003 + ADR-005 slice 4 (where B2 was actually implemented).
- Migration guide if the project convention requires one for PyBot-visible API additions — check `docs/migration-guides/` for the established pattern and follow it only if one exists for "PyO3 surface additions"; otherwise skip (this is purely additive, not a breaking change).

## Validation Gates
- `just lint` clean (markdown lint, if configured).
- Manual: `grep` for `unregister_pool` finds it in the right docs.

## Goal
- Record the B1/B2/B3 decision (B2 settled) + the register/unregister seam design as ADR-007, closing the "decision this session must make" branch of IESD3L.

## Completion note

Landed as commit `e99da91`. New `docs/adr/ADR-007-pool-unregister-seam.md` + a Related-section cross-link from ADR-003.

**Decisions recorded (U1/U2/U3):**
- **U1 — B2 settled.** Construction shape is the Python-companion-wraps-`PyLiquidityPool` pattern ADR-005 Slice 4 already implemented (`builders/v2_pool_builder.py:146` etc., `engine_registry.py:147-151`). The IESD3L B1/B2/B3 option matrix is closed, retained only as historical context. B1 breaks library callers; B3 is larger-blast-radius cleanup not needed for correctness — neither revisited.
- **U2 — refusal-on-panic stays.** `BotState::register_v2/v3/v4_pool` keep `panic!`/`Err` on duplicate; do *not* become idempotent. Rationale: `EngineRegistry._v*_keys` cache address→pool_id *because* the engine shares `BotState` and can't re-register; the panic is the double-registration detector those caches rely on (ADR-006 D3 "engine never constructs pools"). Idempotent register would mask the divergent state `test_pool_remove_and_recreate` exists to probe.
- **U3 — `unregister_pool` seam.** `BotState::unregister_pool(address, pool_id: Option<PoolId>) -> bool` + `PyBot::unregister_pool` PyO3 (`#[pyo3(signature = (address, pool_id=None))]`). V2/V3 path keys off `address` (resolves via `pool_addresses`); V4 path keys off `(address=pool_manager, pool_id)` (resolves via `v4_pool_ids` — address alone is ambiguous for V4 since one PoolManager hosts many pool ids). Disposes: drops the `PoolEntry` (journal dropped with it → restore for a removed pool is a no-op target), drains matching `v3_buffer`/`v4_buffer` events (else re-register replays stale Mint/Burn/ModifyLiquidity). Returns `true`/`false` (silent on miss, mirroring Python `PoolRegistry.remove`). **`next_pool_id` is not reused** — retired ids stay retired to prevent stale `PyLiquidityPool` handles aliasing to a different pool on recreate.

**Sigma for the buffer API (matters for T2/G2TGP6):** `LiquidityEventBuffer` (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/optimizers/liquidity_event_buffer.rs`) has `buffer_backfill`/`buffer_pump`/`drain_backfill`/`drain_pump`/`event_count`/`flush`/`expire` but **no per-key discard**. U3 calls for adding `discard_for(&mut self, key: &K)` — the symmetric inverse of the buffer methods, single-key variant of `flush`. T2 must implement this.

**Engine-side unregister deferred (recorded in ADR-007 Consequences + Deferred):** `EngineRegistry._v2_keys`/`_v3_keys`/`_v4_keys` cache stale `address→pool_id` after a remove going through `bot.pools.remove`. No caller/test exercises remove/recreate through the engine today. Out of scope for IESD3L; the engine-side `unregister_pool` + per-path invalidation is the matching half of ADR-006 D3 for removal, tracked for a future cleanup.

**Validation:** `just lint` green (rust fmt + clippy, ruff, ty, markdownlint 190 files 0 errors). All cited paths verified to exist; line-number cites verified accurate.

Ready: T2 (G2TGP6 — Rust implementation) is the next ready child of IESD3L.

## Goal
- Add `BotState::unregister_pool` (V2/V3-address + V4-tuple paths), `LiquidityEventBuffer::discard_for`, and `PyBot::unregister_pool` (V2/V3 only — V4 lives on the engine, deferred) so removal propagates to Rust-owned state. Implements ADR-007 (task 223IU3).

## Context
- `BotState` (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/bot_core/mod.rs`) holds pools in three maps: `pools: HashMap<u64, PoolEntry>`, `pool_addresses: HashMap<Address, u64>` (V2/V3), `v4_pool_ids: HashMap<(Address, PoolId), u64>` (V4). Plus `next_pool_id` (not reused — removed IDs are retired to avoid stale-handle aliasing) and the `v3_buffer`/`v4_buffer` `LiquidityEventBuffer`s holding events for unregistered pools.
- `register_v2/v3/v4_pool` `panic!`/`Err` on duplicate address; that behavior stays (ADR-007 U2).
- `PyBot` (`rust/src/py_bot.rs`) exposes `register_v2_pool` + `register_v3_pool` but **NOT** `register_v4_pool` — V4 registration lives on `UniswapArbEngine` in `rust/src/py_binding.rs:1332`. So `PyBot::unregister_pool` handles V2/V3 only; the V4 `(pool_manager, pool_id)` path lands on `BotState::unregister_pool` now (for when the engine-side unregister arrives) but is not wired through `PyBot` in this slice. This was confirmed during T2 setup and ADR-007's U3 was updated to match; the engine-side V4 + `_v4_keys` cleanup is the deferred work already recorded in ADR-007 Consequences + Deferred.
- ADR-005: reorg journals (`V2BlockDelta`, V3/V4 `V3BlockDelta` shape) live on `PoolEntry`. Removed entry = journal dropped with it.
- `LiquidityEventBuffer` (`rust/crates/degenbot-bot/src/optimizers/liquidity_event_buffer.rs`) exposes `buffer_backfill`/`buffer_pump`/`drain_backfill`/`drain_pump`/`event_count`/`flush`/`expire` but **no per-key discard** — add `discard_for(&mut self, key: &K)` (single-key inverse of `flush`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `LiquidityEventBuffer::discard_for(&mut self, key: &K)` — drops all buffered events for one key (both backfill + pump). Symmetric inverse of `buffer_pump(key, …)`/`buffer_backfill(key, …)`; single-key variant of `flush()`. Covered by a buffer-level unit test in the `liquidity_event_buffer` module.
- `BotState::unregister_pool(&mut self, address: Address, pool_id: Option<PoolId>) -> bool`:
  - V2/V3 path (`pool_id` is None): if `pool_addresses` has `address`, remove from `pools` and `pool_addresses`. If V3, also `v3_buffer.discard_for(&address)`. Return `true` if removed, `false` if not found.
  - V4 path (`pool_id` is Some): the `address` arg is the PoolManager address. If `v4_pool_ids` has `(address, pool_id)`, remove from `pools`, `v4_pool_ids`, and `v4_buffer.discard_for(&(address, pool_id))`. Return `true`/`false`.
  - Does **not** reuse `next_pool_id` — retired IDs stay retired.
  - Silent no-op returning `false` on unknown.
- `PyBot::unregister_pool(&self, address: &str, pool_id: Option<Vec<u8>>) -> PyResult<bool>` — `#[pyo3(signature = (address, pool_id=None))]`. **V2/V3 path only** (matches `PyBot`'s V2/V3 register surface — V4 is engine-side). Parses address; panics-on-miss is NOT used — returns `Ok(false)` on unknown (silent-on-miss matches Python `PoolRegistry.remove`).
- Unit tests in `bot_core/mod.rs` test module:
  - V2: register → unregister → re-register succeeds (no panic), pool_id is a fresh id (≠ first); `unregister_pool` on unknown returns `false`; journal is gone (cannot restore a removed pool_id — `v2_restore_before_block(removed_id, …)` is a no-op like other V2 ops).
  - V3: register → buffer an event for an unregistered sibling address (use `apply_v3_liquidity_update` on a NEVER-registered address so it buffers) → unregister the registered pool → re-register →   assert the buffer entry for that address is empty after unregister via `v3_buffered_event_count(address)`. Actually simpler: register pool A at address X, buffer events for X via `apply_v3_liquidity_update(X, …)` (returns None and buffers), unregister X, assert `v3_buffered_event_count(X) == 0`.
  - V4: register → unregister by `(pool_manager, pool_id)` → re-register succeeds; buffered ModifyLiquidity discarded (mirror V3 test using `apply_v4_liquidity_update` on a registered-then-unregistered key).
  - `unregister_pool` on never-registered address returns `false`, no mutation (pool_count unchanged).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` green (new tests included).
- `just lint-rust` clean (no new clippy drift).
- `just fmt-check` clean.
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores` OK (PyBot lives in root `rust/src/`, not a core crate).

## Goal
- Add `BotState::unregister_pool` (V2/V3-address + V4-tuple paths), `LiquidityEventBuffer::discard_for`, and `PyBot::unregister_pool` (V2/V3 only — V4 lives on the engine, deferred) so removal propagates to Rust-owned state. Implements ADR-007 (task 223IU3).

## Completion note

Landed as commit `5922f5bf`. All 4 validation gates green: fmt-check EXIT 0, lint-rust EXIT 0, check-no-pyo3-in-cores OK, test-rust EXIT 0, test-rust-python 211 passed.

**Delivered:**
- `LiquidityEventBuffer::discard_for(&mut self, key: &K)` — per-key inverse of `flush()`; drops backfill+pump events for one key. Silent no-op on unknown (matches `drain_*`).
- `BotState::unregister_pool(address, pool_id: Option<PoolId>) -> bool` — V2/V3 path (None) keyed by `pool_addresses`; V4 path (Some) keyed by `(address=pool_manager, pool_id)` via `v4_pool_ids`. Drops `PoolEntry` (journal dropped with it). Drains `v3_buffer`/`v4_buffer` for the key. Silent-on-miss returns `false`. Does NOT reuse `next_pool_id` (retired).
- `PyBot::unregister_pool(address, pool_id=None) -> bool` — V2/V3 path only. A `Some(pool_id)` raises `ValueError` (V4 is engine-side).

**ADR-007 U3 amended during implementation (commit also updates ADR-007):** the original task body assumed `PyBot` exposes a V4 `register_v4_pool` — it does not. V4 registration lives on `UniswapArbEngine` (`rust/src/py_binding.rs:1332`). So `PyBot::unregister_pool` handles V2/V3 only; the V4 `(pool_manager, pool_id)` removal belongs on the engine, alongside the engine-side `_v4_keys`/per-path cleanup already flagged as out-of-scope in ADR-007 Consequences/Deferred. `BotState::unregister_pool` itself takes the V4 tuple path (for when the engine-side unregister lands); `PyBot` just doesn't expose it.

**TDD (Red/Green):** 4 `BotState` tests + 2 `LiquidityEventBuffer` tests written red first (failed to compile with E0599 "no method named unregister_pool/discard_for"), then green after implementation:
- `unregister_v2_pool_returns_true_then_re_register_allocates_fresh_id` — proves retired-id-not-reused (the load-bearing safety property).
- `unregister_pool_on_unknown_address_returns_false_silently` — silent-on-miss contract.
- `unregister_v3_pool_discards_buffered_liquidity_events` — buffers pre-registration via `buffer_backfill_v3_liquidity_update` (registration does NOT auto-drain — drain is caller-driven via `apply_backfill_buffer_v3`), unregisters, asserts `buffered_v3_event_count == 0`.
- `unregister_v4_pool_by_tuple_key_discards_buffered_modify_liquidity` — register → unregister by tuple → re-register succeeds with fresh id.
- `discard_for_clears_backfill_and_pump_for_one_key` / `discard_for_on_unknown_key_is_a_silent_no_op` — buffer-level contract.

**Python-side smoke verified** (not a committed test, just a runtime check): `PyBot().register_v2_pool(...)` → `unregister_pool` returns `True`, `pool_count` drops to 0; second `unregister_pool` on the removed address returns `False`; `pool_id=b'\\xee'*32` raises `ValueError`.

**Baseline drift also fixed in this pass:** `liquidity_event_buffer.rs:52` `#[must_use]` on `new()` (pre-existing, surfaced because `just lint-rust --fix` touches the file).

**Ready: T3 (PDRB42 — Python wire).** The seam now exists at `PyBot.unregister_pool(address, pool_id=None) -> bool`. T3's job: add `py_bot: PyBot | None` to `PoolRegistry.__init__`, wire `remove`/`reset` + `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove` to call it, and pass `py_bot=self._py_bot` from `Bot.__init__` (`bot.py:133`). The acceptance test `test_pool_remove_and_recreate` should then pass.

## Goal
- Wire Python `PoolRegistry.remove`/`reset` + `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove` → `PyBot.unregister_pool` so the Python↔Rust state seam stays symmetric with the builder's `add` direction. Unblocks `test_uniswap_trackers.py::test_pool_remove_and_recreate`.

## Completion note

Landed as commit `352ebc9a`. All gates green: fmt-check, lint (ruff + ty + markdownlint + clippy), test-rust, test-rust-python (211), and the full Python suite **3147 passed, 0 failed** (the 3 previously-failing tests now green, zero regressions).

**Delivered:**
- `PoolRegistry.__init__` gains keyword-only `py_bot: PyBot | None = None`. When `None` (standalone test constructions, all ~10 test sites) removal stays Python-only — no behavior change. `Bot.__init__` + `AsyncBot.__init__` pass `py_bot=self._py_bot`.
- `PoolRegistry.remove` V2/V3 path (no bytes `pool_id`) calls `py_bot.unregister_pool(address=pool_address)` before the Python `_remove`. V4 path (bytes `pool_id`) stays Python-only — V4 unregister is engine-side (ADR-007 Deferred).
- `PoolRegistry._reset()` iterates **storage keys** (`(chain_id, address)` tuples — the second element is the checksummed contract address) rather than pool objects. This is robust against test mocks (`object()` without `.address` — the regression I hit in `test_release_resets_pool_and_token_registries` during the first pass). Calls `unregister_pool` for each before clearing.
- `degenbot_rs.pyi` stub: added `unregister_pool(address, pool_id=...) -> bool` so `ty` resolves the PyO3 method (the stub is the single source of truth for the compiled extension's Python surface).
- `ManagedPoolRegistry.remove` NOT propagated — V4 is engine-side per ADR-007's U3 amendment (T2 discovery: `PyBot` exposes only V2/V3; V4 registration lives on `UniswapArbEngine`).

**Acceptance test green:** `test_pool_remove_and_recreate` — `bot.pools.remove(...)` now propagates to Rust `BotState`; the third `get_pool_from_tokens` re-build succeeds instead of panicking `pool already registered`.

**Regression caught and fixed during the pass:** `test_release_resets_pool_and_token_registries` seeds the registry with `object()` mocks (no `.address`). First implementation iterated `self.list_all()` and accessed `pool.address` — `AttributeError`. Fixed by iterating `self._storage()` keys (the checksummed address is in the key, not the value). This is actually more correct: the key's address is the canonical checksummed form used for both Python lookup and Rust registration.

**Ready: T4 (3K4ZQF — Docs sync).** Sync `rust/CONTEXT.md`, `rust/AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT-MAP.md` with the `unregister_pool` seam; cross-link ADR-007 (already done in T1's ADR-003 edit; T4 adds the layered-module docs).

## Goal
- Sync the layered docs (`rust/CONTEXT.md`, `rust/AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT-MAP.md`) so the unregister seam is discoverable, and cross-link ADR-007 from ADR-003's "in scope here" branch.

## Completion note

Landed as commit `22e67ea1`. All gates green: markdownlint (190 files, 0 errors), fmt-check, lint-context-maps EXIT 0, and the 5 IESD3L acceptance tests re-confirmed green.

The ADR-003→ADR-007 cross-link landed earlier in T1's commit (`e99da91`). T4 is the layered-module sync:

- **`rust/CONTEXT.md`** (3 edits):
  - **`PyBot`** term: method list now includes `unregister_pool`; documents V2/V3-only on `PyBot` (V4 engine-side), the retired-id discipline (`next_pool_id` never reused), and the `pool_id` set raising on `PyBot`.
  - **`Reorg Journal`** term: annotated that `BotState::unregister_pool` (ADR-007) drops the `PoolEntry` + its journal together → restore for a removed `pool_id` is a no-op target; pump reorg detection naturally skips removed pools (the address/id no longer resolves).
  - **New `Unregister Seam (ADR-007)` term**: the symmetric removal half of register — V2/V3 address-keyed vs V4 `(pool_manager, pool_id)`-keyed; discards `v3_buffer`/`v4_buffer` events via `LiquidityEventBuffer::discard_for`; silent-on-miss `false`; `register` stays refusal-on-`panic!`/`Err` (the asymmetry reflects invariant asymmetry, not inconsistency — ADR-007 U2); the Python seam (`PoolRegistry.__init__` `py_bot` kwarg + `remove`/`_reset` propagation).
  - New **Relationships bullet**: `PyBot` → `BotState::unregister_pool`, noting `LiquidityEventBuffer::discard_for` as the single-key inverse of `flush`.
- **`rust/AGENTS.md`**: `py_bot.rs` table row updated — notes the symmetric removal half, retired-not-reused pool_ids (`next_pool_id` only advances), and V4-deferred-to-engine.
- **`CONTEXT-MAP.md`**: Rust Extension bullet extended with the Unregister Seam (ADR-007) summary — V2/V3 on `PyBot`, V4 engine-side, deferred.

**No migration guide** — per the established pattern (`docs/migration-guides/dex-subclass-collapse.md` is "breaking (0.x)"), migration guides record breaking changes only. The `unregister_pool` addition is purely additive: a new PyO3 method + a new optional `py_bot` kwarg defaulting to `None`. No existing API surface changed; no back-compat alias needed (AGENTS.md "design standalone features without a backwards compatibility layer" — though this isn't standalone, it's additive, so the same no-shim conclusion holds).

**Cross-link verification:** `grep -l unregister_pool` finds it in all five expected docs (`rust/CONTEXT.md`, `rust/AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT-MAP.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-007-*.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-003-*.md`).

**IESD3L epic complete** — all 4 children done (223IU3 ADR-007, G2TGP6 Rust, PDRB42 Python, 3K4ZQF Docs). The failing test `test_pool_remove_and_recreate` is unblocked; the full Python suite is green (3147 passed, 0 failed); the full Rust workspace test + PyO3-wrapped tests + all lint/format gates are green. The two ADR-007-deferred items (engine-side V4 unregister + `_v*_keys` cache invalidation, and `ManagedPoolRegistry._reset` parity) are recorded in ADR-007's Consequences/Deferred for a future cleanup if/when a caller exercises remove/recreate through the engine.

data.title: ADR-006 slice 8b: Bot/AsyncBot single-chain facade (in-progress stash@{0})
data.body:
## Goal
- Land ADR-006 slice 8b: collapse `bot.py`/`async_bot.py` into single-chain facades (one `ProviderAdapter`/`AsyncProviderAdapter` per Bot, chain identity from `config.default_chain_id`), retiring the multi-chain `ConnectionManager`/`AsyncConnectionManager`.

## Context
- ADR-006 D5 decides the direction: "One `Bot` per chain; multi-chain is N Bots." `bot.py` is today multi-chain "by accident" — it swallowed a `ConnectionManager`/`AsyncConnectionManager` and pool/token managers across chains. The ADR calls for unwinding that into a single-chain facade.
- The codebase already references this slice by name: `rust/src/py_bot.rs:111` ("`chain_id = 0` placeholder until ADR-006 slice 8 makes `bot.py` a single-chain facade") and `src/degenbot/registry/CONTEXT.md:22` ("`pool_registry`/`token_registry`/`managed_pool_registry` (Removed under ADR-006 slice 8b): formerly module-level singletons; now Bot-owned class instances"). So slice 8b is the *named* future home for this work.
- This is **not** any of the ADR-005 "Slice N" ergo tasks (R3ZAUV etc. — those are the companion-class ports: Slice 7=DEX collapse, 8=V3 companion, 9=V4 companion, …). This is ADR-006's slice numbering; the names collide but the bodies are unrelated.

## The in-progress artifact

**`git stash@{0}`** holds partway-done work for this slice. Stash subject: `slice-8-inprogress: bot/async_bot single-chain rewrite (sync working, async enforcement + cascade TODO)`. Touches 6 files (~290 LoC delta):

- `src/degenbot/bot.py` — single-chain rewrite (sync path reported working)
- `src/degenbot/async_bot.py` — single-chain rewrite (async enforcement + cascade still TODO per the author)
- `src/degenbot/connection/connection_manager.py` — multi-chain manager shrink
- `src/degenbot/provider/factory.py` — provider factory retarget
- `tests/helpers/bot_factory.py` — test helper updates
- `tests/test_bot.py` — test updates

The stash was left in the repo's stash list at start of session (not created this session). It is **not** tracked by IESD3L or any prior ergo task — it's an orphan work-in-progress. This task is its discoverable home.

## Known conflict against current HEAD

The stash will **not** pop cleanly. It conflicts with `src/degenbot/bot.py` and `src/degenbot/async_bot.py` around the `PoolRegistry()` constructor call: the stash changes `Bot.__init__` to pass `default_chain_id=self._chain_id` (its single-chain wiring) on lines adjacent to where IESD3L's T3 (`352ebc9a`) added `py_bot=self._py_bot`. A straight `git stash pop` will hit a text conflict on both files. Resolution is mechanical: keep both changes (the `default_chain_id=` from the stash AND the `py_bot=` from IESD3L) — they're orthogonal constructor args. Confirmed during the IESD3L pass when a `stash pop` was attempted for an unrelated fmt-baseline check and conflicted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `bot.py` and `async_bot.py` are single-chain facades: one provider per Bot, `chain_id` sourced from `config.default_chain_id`, the multi-chain `ConnectionManager`/`AsyncConnectionManager` retired or scoped out of the Bot's direct surface.
- The `chain_id = 0` placeholder in `rust/src/py_bot.rs:111` resolves to the real chain id (per ADR-006 D4: `Bot::new(chain_id)`).
- `tests/test_bot.py` + `tests/helpers/bot_factory.py` updated to the single-chain shape.
- The async path lands the "enforcement + cascade" TODO the stash author flagged (sync is reported working; async is the unfinished half).
- `just test-all` green (Rust workspace + PyO3-wrapped + Python).
- Stash `stash@{0}` is dropped once its content is committed (the work has a real commit history instead of living in the stash list).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-all`
- `just lint`
- `just fmt-check`

## Out of scope
- IESD3L's unregister seam (already landed) — this task should preserve the `PoolRegistry(py_bot=self._py_bot)` wiring from commit `352ebc9a` while resolving the stash conflict.
- The ADR-005 "Slice N" companion-class ports (R3ZAUV, DULSSU, etc.) — different slice-numbering scheme, unrelated.

## Goal
- Eliminate the `rust/src/subscription.rs` ↔ `crates/degenbot-rpc/src/subscription.rs`
  name collision (and any other duplicates found by audit) so the binding layer reliably
  signals "this is the PyO3 side" by file name.

  per-domain subdir move.

## Context
- ADR-005's naming rule: the `Py` prefix is kept on the PyO3 wrapper struct AND as a
  Python-exposed name; the bare noun is reserved for the Rust core. By extension, a
  binding-side file should not collide in name with a core-crate file.
- `rust/AGENTS.md` already states the GIL-bound half of subscription moved to
  `subscription_py.rs` in slice 5 — but `rust/src/subscription.rs` still exists and is
  756 lines (GIL-bound, imports `crate::py_converters::*`).
- Other files to audit for the same pattern: anything in `rust/src/` whose stem matches a
  file in `crates/degenbot-*/src/`. (`provider_py.rs` vs `provider.rs` already follows the
  convention — check the rest.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- `rust/src/subscription.rs` is renamed to `subscription_py.rs` (interim — matches the
  current `*_py.rs` convention; the per-domain subdir move in step 6 will relocate it to

data.title: Extract #[pymodule] registration into rust/src/c_api.rs
data.body:
## Goal
- Pull the `#[pymodule] fn degenbot` body out of `rust/src/lib.rs` into a dedicated
  `rust/src/c_api.rs` so `lib.rs` is a thin module-tree + re-export file.
- Establish the single place future `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pyclass]` registrations land —
  matches `polars-python/src/c_api/mod.rs`.

## Context
- Today `rust/src/lib.rs` (217 lines) mixes three jobs: module docstring, ~80 lines of
  `pub use degenbot_*::…` re-exports, and a growing `#[pymodule]` body of
  `m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(...))?` + `m.add_class::<...>()?` lines.
- Polars puts all 159 registration calls in `c_api/mod.rs`, gated `#[cfg(feature="c_api")]`;
  the binding crate's `lib.rs` is tiny (module declarations + types).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New file `rust/src/c_api.rs` exporting `pub fn register(m: &Bound<PyModule>) -> PyResult<()>`
  containing every existing `m.add_function(...)` and `m.add_class::<...>()` call, in the
  same order as today.
- `rust/src/lib.rs` `#[pymodule] fn degenbot(_py, m) -> PyResult<()>` body reduced to a single
  call: `c_api::register(m)` (plus any module-level `m.add(...)` for submodules/exceptions that
  must run before/after — preserved with their relative order; anything that genuinely must be
  in the module init stays in `lib.rs` with a comment explaining why).
- No change to which functions/classes are registered or to their Python-visible names.
- `lib.rs` keeps the existing `pub use degenbot_*::…` re-exports unchanged (call sites depend
  on them).

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just test-rust-python`
- `uv run python -c "import degenbot_rs; from degenbot_rs import PyBot; print('ok')"`
- Diff sanity: the set of `add_function`/`add_class` calls in `c_api.rs` equals the set that
  was in `lib.rs` before (count + names match).

data.title: Add conversion/ subdir for shared PyO3-dependent converters
data.body:
## Goal
- Carve `alloy_py.rs`, `py_cache.rs`, `json_converters.rs`, `py_converters.rs` out of the
  flat `rust/src/` layout into a shared `rust/src/conversion/` subdir.
- Establish the `polars-python/src/conversion/` analogue: PyO3-dependent glue used by many
  wrappers, exposing no `#[pyfunction]` of its own.

## Context
- `rust/AGENTS.md` already names this as a category: "PyO3-dependent converters (no
  `#[pyfunction]`, but creates Python objects)" — examples `py_converters.rs`, `alloy_py.rs`,
  `py_cache.rs`. The current flat layout buries them among `#[pyfunction]` wrappers.
- Polars: `conversion/{any_value,categorical,chunked_array,datetime}.rs` + a root
  `Wrap<T>` newtype (`pub type PySchema = Wrap<polars_core::schema::Schema>;`).
- Current sizes for sizing: `py_converters.rs` 697, `alloy_py.rs` 335, `json_converters.rs`
  196, `py_cache.rs` 194. No logic changes — purely move + re-export.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `rust/src/conversion/` dir with:
  - `mod.rs` declaring + `pub use`-ing each submodule
  - `alloy.rs`     (was `alloy_py.rs`)
  - `cache.rs`     (was `py_cache.rs`)
  - `json.rs`      (was `json_converters.rs`)
  - `rpc_types.rs` (was `py_converters.rs`)
- All existing `use crate::alloy_py::…`, `use crate::py_cache::…`,
