data.title: Add rust/src/prelude.rs and migrate wrapper use blocks
data.body:
## Goal
- Add a binding-crate `prelude.rs` mirroring `polars-python/src/prelude.rs` so wrapper files
  open with `use crate::prelude::*;` instead of ~10–15 lines of repeated imports.
- Migrate the `use` blocks of every `*_py.rs` wrapper to use the prelude.

## Context
- Polars prelude (3 lines): `pub use polars::prelude::*; pub use crate::conversion::*; pub(crate) use crate::py_modules;`.
- Today each degenbot wrapper file repeats `use pyo3::prelude::*;`, `use crate::alloy_py::*;`
  (now `crate::conversion::alloy` post step 3), `use crate::py_converters::*;`, `use degenbot_core::*`,
  `use crate::py_cache::*;` etc.
- Depends on step 3 (`conversion/` subdir): the prelude re-exports `crate::conversion::*`, so
  it must land after the conversion paths are stable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `rust/src/prelude.rs` re-exporting at minimum: `pyo3::prelude::*`, the conversion
  submodule surface (`crate::conversion::*`), and `degenbot_core` surface used across wrappers.
- Keep it small — no `pub use *` of rarely-used items; aim for the smallest set that covers
  every wrapper's repeated imports (justify any item that's added but used in only one wrapper
  — those should stay as local `use`s).
- Every `*_py.rs` wrapper file's top-of-file `use` block reduced to `use crate::prelude::*;`
  (plus `use super::*;` and any file-specific imports); no behavior change.
- Gated/duplicate imports removed (no file imports a prelude item *and* the prelude).

## Validation Gates
- `just lint-rust` (clean)
- `just test-rust`
- `just test-rust-python`
- Manual spot-check: pick 3 wrapper files and confirm the `use` block is now ≤ ~3 lines plus
  file-specific imports.

data.title: Split py_binding.rs per the uniswap_engine/ core layout
data.body:
## Goal
- Break `rust/src/py_binding.rs` (3012 lines, one `#[pyclass] PyUniswapArbEngine` with 100+
  methods + several `#[create_exception]` types + helper impls) into a per-concern file set
  under `rust/src/bot/engine/`, mirroring the existing
  `crates/degenbot-bot/src/optimizers/uniswap_engine/` split.
- Use PyO3's support for multiple `#[pymethods] impl PyX { … }` blocks per type — declare
  the struct once, drop one `#[pymethods]` impl per concern.

## Context
- This is the highest-judgment step in the migration; the others are mechanical renames.
- Polars precedent: `PyExpr` split across 17 files (`expr/{array,binary,string,list,datetime,
  rolling,meta,…}.rs`), each holding one `#[pymethods] impl PyExpr { … }` block. `PyDataFrame`
  split across `dataframe/{general,io,construction,map,export,serde}.rs`. Core struct declared
  once in `mod.rs` alongside `From`/`Clone`/`new` (non-py helpers only).
- degenbot's core already factored `uniswap_engine` into
  `{diagnostic,event_routing,solver_dispatch,lifecycle,snapshot_verify,result_channel}.rs` —
  mirror those names in the binding layer so the split is "obvious from the core".

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `rust/src/bot/engine/` directory (note: created flat in `rust/src/bot/engine/` here;
  step 6 will relocate the surrounding `bot/` files alongside — keep `engine/` self-contained
  so step 6 moves it as a unit):
  - `mod.rs` — the `#[pyclass] struct PyUniswapArbEngine` declaration, `From`/`Clone`/helper
    (non-py) impl blocks, and `pub use`/`mod` declarations for the sibling files.
  - `register.rs` — `#[pymethods]` block: `register_pool`, `register_path`, `start`, `stop`,
    `freeze` (registration + lifecycle-entry surface).
  - `solve.rs` — `#[pymethods]` block: `solve_dirty`, `process_logs`, `latest_results`, any
    result-retrieval surface.
  - `verify.rs` — `#[pymethods]` block: all `verify_*` methods + the `VerifyRpc` /
    `EngineVerifyRpc` impls + the `verify_*_rejected` exception types they raise.
  - `snapshot.rs` — `#[pymethods]` block: snapshot_* surface (mirrors core `snapshot_verify.rs`).
  - `result_channel.rs` — `#[pymethods]` block: result-channel surface (mirrors core
    `result_channel.rs`).
  - `errors.rs` — all `#[create_exception]` types currently in `py_binding.rs`.
- `rust/src/py_binding.rs` deleted; `lib.rs` / `c_api.rs` registration rewritten to point at
  `crate::bot::engine::PyUniswapArbEngine`.
- Any cross-file helper used by multiple concern-files kept in `mod.rs` as `pub(crate)`.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just test-rust-python` — especially the engine / arb-solve test suites.
- `just lint-rust`
- Manual: every `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pymethods]` symbol previously exposed is still exposed
  (diff the `#[pymodule]` registration set before/after; must be identical).
- Confirm `#[pymethods]` is not duplicated for the same method (PyO3 errors at build time, but
  also grep to verify).

data.title: Move binding-layer files into per-domain subdirs
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace the flat `rust/src/*.rs` layout with per-domain subdirs mirroring the seven core
  crates, per technique 1 — the umbrella mechanical rename that supersedes the `*_py.rs`
  filename convention inside the binding crate.

## Context
- Target layout lives in `BINDING-LAYER-REORG.md` ("Target layout" section). Source mapping:
  `rust/src/bot/` ↔ `crates/degenbot-bot/`, `rust/src/abi/` ↔ `crates/degenbot-abi/`, etc.
- Depends on steps 1–5 so that file identities are final (subscription_py renamed, c_api
  extracted, conversion subdir in place, prelude landing, py_binding already split into
  `bot/engine/`) — moving anything earlier fights in-flight renames.
- The `*_py.rs` filename convention is **dropped inside the binding crate**: every file there
  is "py" by default; the crate boundary (workspace split / `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`)
  is the separator that matters. Polars precedent: only one `*_py.rs` file in all of
  `polars-python/src/`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Files relocated, renamed per the target layout in `BINDING-LAYER-REORG.md`:
  - `py_bot.rs` → `bot/mod.rs`, `py_liquidity_pool.rs` → `bot/pool.rs`,
    `py_erc20_token.rs` → `bot/token.rs`, `py_dex_identity.rs` → `bot/dex_identity.rs`.
  - `bot/engine/` (from step 5) moved alongside as a subdir.
  - `abi_decoder_py.rs` → `abi/decoder.rs`, `abi_encoder_py.rs` → `abi/encoder.rs`.
  - `tick_math_py.rs` → `cl_math/tick_math.rs`, `cl_lib_py.rs` → `cl_math/cl_lib.rs`.
  - `provider_py.rs` → `rpc/provider.rs`, `contract_py.rs` → `rpc/contract.rs`,
    `subscription_py.rs` → `rpc/subscription.rs`, `async_provider.rs` → `rpc/async_provider.rs`,
    `async_contract.rs` → `rpc/async_contract.rs`.
  - `address_utils_py.rs` → `uniswap/address.rs`.
  - `lib.rs`, `c_api.rs`, `prelude.rs`, `conversion/` stay at root.
- Every `use crate::…` and `mod …` reference updated across `rust/src/`.
- `c_api.rs` `add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(<path>, m))` paths updated to the new module paths;
  `add_class::<…>` paths likewise.
- `rust/AGENTS.md` "Module Organization" / "Module Naming Convention" table updated to reflect
  the new layout (drop the blanket `*_py.rs` rule for the root cdylib; note that the rule now
  applies only to any future standalone binding crate that mixes pyo3 with shared converters).
- `rust/CONTEXT.md` PyO3-handle terms updated if they reference file paths.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust`
- `just test-rust-python`
- `just lint-rust`
- `just check-no-pyo3-in-cores`
- `uv run python -c "import degenbot_rs; from degenbot_rs import PyBot, PyLiquidityPool, PyUniswapArbEngine; print('ok')"`
- Manual: confirm no `*_py.rs` files remain in `rust/src/` except inside `conversion/` if there
  are any genuine conversion-only modules named that way (there shouldn't be).

data.title: Add binding-crate cargo features mirroring core crates
data.body:
## Goal
- Add `degenbot_rs` (the root cdylib binding layer) cargo features gating each `dep:` path
  dependency and matching `#[cfg(feature="...")]` on the corresponding binding module, so a
  consumer can build the extension with a subset of surfaces.
- This is the action that most directly prepares for the ADR-005 deferral (binding crate
  becomes its own workspace member, `degenbot-python`).

## Context
- Polars gates `polars-python` with features (`pymethods`, `c_api`, `sql`, `catalog`, …)
  mirroring `polars-core`/`-plan`/etc. one-to-one; `#[cfg(feature="pymethods")] mod general;`.
- degenbot's core crates today carry only a `pyo3`/`test-utils` feature each (per
  `rust/AGENTS.md`); the root `degenbot_rs` cdylib is monolithic — no binding-layer features.
- This is **additive**: default features preserve today's behavior exactly; the work is
  inserting `cfg` gates + feature deps without changing what ships by default.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `[features]` in `rust/Cargo.toml` defines (default all-on):
  ```
  default = ["bot", "rpc", "abi", "cl-math", "uniswap"]
  bot      = ["dep:degenbot-bot"]
  rpc      = ["dep:degenbot-rpc"]
  abi      = ["dep:degenbot-abi"]
  cl-math  = ["dep:degenbot-cl-math"]
  uniswap  = ["dep:degenbot-uniswap"]
  decoders = ["dep:degenbot-decoders"]
  async    = []    # gates rpc/async_provider.rs + rpc/async_contract.rs (no new dep)
  ```
- Each path dep moved under `[features]` accordingly (already-path-deps remain path deps,
  just optionally enabled).
- `#[cfg(feature = "bot")] pub mod bot;` (etc.) in `lib.rs`, and each domain `mod.rs` gates
  its submodule declarations where the feature would not be on.
- `c_api.rs` registration of classes/functions gated so a build with a feature off doesn't
  reference symbols that aren't compiled (e.g. `#[cfg(feature = "bot")] m.add_class::<PyBot>()?;`).
- **Default build is byte-equivalent in surface** to today: `cargo build` with defaults
  produces the same `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pyclass]` set.
- An audit note in the completion body: any implicit cross-feature coupling discovered
  (e.g. "engine wrapper imports subscribe from rpc even though engine uses an injected pump")
  and a recommendation per finding.

## Validation Gates
- `just test-rust` (default features)
- `just test-rust-python` (default features)
- `just lint-rust`
- `cargo build -p degenbot_rs --no-default-features --features bot` succeeds (and a couple
  of other minimal feature combinations).
- `cargo build -p degenbot_rs --no-default-features` fails cleanly at build (no missing-symbol
  panics at runtime) — confirm the error messages point at the gated symbols.
- `uv run python -c "import degenbot_rs; print('ok')"` (default features, byte-equivalent).

## Plan

Implements `plans/101-v3-v4-pool-handle-companions.md` slice 8. Parent epic:
`XQ5UX6` (Polars three-layer migration — ADR-005).

## Goal

Rewrite `UniswapV3Pool` as a thin Python companion over the existing
`PyLiquidityPool` handle (the V2 template from ADR-005 slice 4/5). Rust
`BotState` becomes the single source of truth for V3 mutable state (scalars,
tick data, reorg journal) — matching V2 exactly. The example registers V3 pools
**once** via `PyBot.register_v3_pool`, the engine reads through that state via
`register_and_solve_path`, and the example drops the ~10-field re-registration +
the duplicate DB-snapshot load (the engine `load_v3_snapshot` /
`stream_v3_snapshot_to_engine` path remains the sole tick source).

## Sub-slices (vertical, smallest-first)

- **8a (Rust surface)**: V3 family of pymethods on `PyLiquidityPool` (getters
  `sqrt_price_x96`/`liquidity`/`tick`/`update_block`/`fee`/`tick_spacing`,
  `snapshot_v3`, `apply_swap`, `apply_liquidity_update`, `update_tick_data`,
  journal ops `discard_before_block`/`restore_before_block`, snapshot getters
  `tick_data`/`tick_bitmap`); add `BotState::apply_v3_swap_by_pool_id` +
  `apply_v3_liquidity_update_by_pool_id`; extend `PyBot.register_v3_pool` to
  return `PyLiquidityPool` (currently `u64`). Red→green: extend
  `tests/arbitrage/test_optimizers/test_shared_state_topology.py` with a V3
  round-trip mirroring the existing V2 test.

- **8b (Python companion)**: rewrite `src/degenbot/uniswap/v3_liquidity_pool.py`
  constructor + property delegations + mutations over `PyLiquidityPool`; drop
  `_state_mgr` / `_state_cache` / `state_cache_depth`. Update existing V3 tests.

- **8c (Builder + example)**: V3 builder routes through `py_bot.register_v3_pool`
  → hand `PyLiquidityPool` to constructor; drop `load_tick_snapshot` DB path.
  Example `EngineRegistry.register_v3_pool` collapses to
  `pool._py_pool.pool_id` (mirror V2). Smoke `examples/eth_backrun_v2_v3_v4_rust.py`
  → reaches `solve_all_paths`.

## Acceptance

- Existing V3 simulation tests stay behaviorally green
- `test_shared_state_topology.py` V3 round-trip passes
- Example end-to-end run reaches `solve_all_paths` with no `engine.register_v3_pool`
  call on the V3 path; no `gc.collect()` of the throwaway Python CL state

## Status

- [x] 8a: Rust `PyLiquidityPool` V3 surface + `register_v3_pool` return-handle
- [ ] 8b: Python `UniswapV3Pool` rewrite
- [ ] 8c: V3 builder + example

## Slice 8a — fully closed (commit a9e8cd89)

Plan-101 slice 8a was landed at commit ce389f62 ("first tracer bullets") but left one
pymethod from the 8a surface list unimplemented: `update_tick_data` (the Python sparse-map
fetcher's write-back path at `src/degenbot/builders/tick_data_fetcher.py:104` calls
`pool.update_tick_data(tick_bitmap, tick_data, block)`). 8a shipped only the read-only
`tick_data_snapshot`/`tick_bitmap_snapshot`. Without a Rust write path, slice 8b's
`update_tick_data` delegation had nowhere to land.

**Closed by** `feat(rust): PyLiquidityPool.update_tick_data write surface` (a9e8cd89):
- `BotState::sync_tick_data_by_pool_id` — pool_id-keyed, family-agnostic (V3+V4 mirror the
  read path's `get_v3_or_v4_pool` + the RAJ3PP apply dispatchers). Replaces the entire
  `tick_data` map; scalars unchanged; `update_block` monotonic (no rewind). No journal
  delta (full-sync, mirrors `sync_v3_pool_state`). Returns false for V2/unregistered.
- `PyLiquidityPool.update_tick_data(tick_bitmap, tick_data, block)` — symmetric with
  `tick_data_snapshot`'s `{tick:(gross,net,block)}` shape; the `tick_bitmap` arg is
  redundant in Rust (bitmap derived from `tick_data` keys) and accepted for API parity.

Red-green TDD: V3 round-trip + V4 mirror pinning the family-agnostic arm (both in
`TestSharedStateTopologyV3`/`V4`). All gates green: `just test-rust`, `just lint-rust`,
`just lint-python`, topology 15 passed.

**Remaining (the actionable bulk):** 8b (Python `UniswapV3Pool` rewrite over the handle —
constructor cutover + scalar/tick/journal property delegations + simulation parity) and 8c
(V3 builder routes through `py_bot.register_v3_pool`; example drops double registration).
8b is a multi-commit undertaking: ~43 `UniswapV3Pool(...)` construction sites across 15
files cutover atomically (mirrors slice 4's ~75-conversion V2 cutover) + a `make_v3_pool`
helper + test rewrites. The `update_tick_data` delegation target now exists; the
`_tick_data_fetcher` write-back path is unblocked. Recommend a focused follow-up session
(fresh context) for 8b+8c, as slice 7's author did for the equivalent-scope collapse.

## Goal
- Eliminate the `rust/src/subscription.rs` ↔ `crates/degenbot-rpc/src/subscription.rs`
  name collision (and any other duplicates found by audit) so the binding layer reliably
  signals "this is the PyO3 side" by file name.
- Unblocks the umbrella rename in step 6 — file identities must be stable before the
  per-domain subdir move.

## Completion note

**Outcome: the collision was a dead orphan.** `rust/src/subscription.rs` (26791 B) was
the pre-split monolith holding both the pure-core `SubscriptionHandle` and the GIL-bound
`PyAlloySubscription`. The Plan-103 crate split moved the pure core to
`crates/degenbot-rpc/src/subscription.rs` and the GIL-bound half to
`rust/src/subscription_py.rs`. The old `rust/src/subscription.rs` was never declared as a
module in `lib.rs` (only `subscription_py` is) — an uncompiled stale duplicate that
collided by name with the core-crate file.

**Action taken: deleted** `rust/src/subscription.rs` (756 lines removed), not renamed.
The rename the task body guessed at had already happened — `subscription_py.rs` already
exists and is the live compiled half. Deleting the dead file is the actual fix.

**Audit (all `rust/src/*.rs` stems vs `crates/degenbot-*/src/*.rs`):**
- Only bare-stem collision was `subscription` (the deleted orphan).
- All other root files use the `_py` suffix convention consistently against their
  core-crate counterparts (`abi_decoder_py`, `abi_encoder_py`, `address_utils_py`,
  `contract_py`, `provider_py`, `subscription_py`). No further collisions.
- Module-tree audit: `lib.rs` declares exactly 19 `pub mod`s; the 19 remaining root
  `.rs` files map 1:1 — no other orphan/dead files.

**`subscription_py.rs::use crate::subscription::SubscriptionHandle`** still resolves
via the existing `pub use degenbot_rpc::{contract, provider, subscription};` re-export.

Commit: `08616afc`.

data.title: Lift binding layer to crates/degenbot-python/ (virtual-manifest workspace)
data.body:
**tags:** `adr-005`, `crate-split`, `binding-layer`, `deferral-executed`, `mechanical-move`, `workspace-restructure`

**Cross-refs:**
- **Predecessor (unblocks this task):** ergo `UKDOUR` (UG6FKN task 7 â binding-crate cargo features; DONE). The per-domain `dep:` features + `#[cfg(feature=...)]` gates added there are what let the binding crate be lifted as a standalone workspace member that depends on a *subset* of cores.
- **Successor (this task is a prerequisite of):** ergo `KWTAXJ` (XQ5UX6 "Slice 13: Crate split â degenbot-core / degenbot-python / umbrella"). KWTAXJ is the broader slice and conflates three concerns; THIS task does only the first (the mechanical relocation + Cargo workspace restructure). The remaining two KWTAXJ concerns â (b) the standalone-`degenbot-core` Rust-consumer smoke test, and (c) the `degenbot` umbrella Python package + `cargo add degenbot` re-export â stay with KWTAXJ.
- **Doc of record:** `BINDING-LAYER-REORG.md` (its "Non-goals" listed this move as deferred; step 7 "prepares for it but does not execute it" â this task executes it). `docs/adr/ADR-005-polars-inspired-three-layer-architecture.md` lines 249â261 (the "Crate split" deferral).

---

## Goal

Lift the `degenbot_rs` binding layer out of the workspace root (`rust/src/`) into a first-class workspace member at `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/`, and convert `rust/Cargo.toml` from a "mixed root" (workspace + package) manifest into a **pure virtual manifest** (workspace only), mirroring the `polars` repo layout where `crates/polars-python/` sits as a peer of `polars-core`/`-ops`/`-plan`/etc. under one virtual-manifest workspace root.

**Pure mechanical relocation + manifest surgery. No behavior change, no API change, no `pub use` re-export churn.** The Python extension module name (`degenbot.degenbot_rs`), the crate/lib name (`degenbot_rs`), and every registered symbol stay byte-identical.

## Why

Today `rust/Cargo.toml` is both the `[workspace]` manifest AND the `degenbot_rs` `[package]` manifest â the "mixed root" Cargo pattern. The seven pyo3-free cores nest under `rust/crates/`, but the binding layer (the thing that *glues* those cores to Python) sits at the workspace *root*. This is the one structural asymmetry vs. the Polars reference project, where everything (binding included) lives under `crates/` and the root is a pure virtual manifest. Lifting the binding layer to a peer of the cores is the move that `UG6FKN` task 7's cargo features were the prep for, and is the ADR-005 "Crate split" deferral's mechanical core.

## Current layout (post-UG6FKN)

```
rust/
  Cargo.toml          # [workspace] + [package] degenbot_rs  (MIXED ROOT)
  src/                 # the binding layer (lib.rs, c_api.rs, prelude.rs,
                       # abi/ bot/ cl_math/ conversion/ rpc/ uniswap/)
  crates/
    degenbot-core/  degenbot-cl-math/  degenbot-abi/  degenbot-rpc/
    degenbot-bot/   degenbot-decoders/ degenbot-uniswap/
```

## Target layout (post-this-task)

```
rust/
  Cargo.toml          # pure VIRTUAL manifest: [workspace] + [profile.*] only
  crates/
    degenbot-python/   # NEW workspace member â the binding layer
      Cargo.toml      # [package] degenbot_rs (name UNCHANGED) + [lib] + [deps] + [features] + [dev-deps] + [[test]]
      src/             # ex-rust/src/  (lib.rs, c_api.rs, prelude.rs, abi/, bot/, cl_math/, conversion/, rpc/, uniswap/)
    degenbot-core/  degenbot-cl-math/  degenbot-abi/  degenbot-rpc/
    degenbot-bot/   degenbot-decoders/ degenbot-uniswap/
```

## Mechanical steps (in order; commit after each green gate)

### Step 1 â Relocate the source tree (single `git mv`)

```bash
cd /home/ralph/code/degenbot
mkdir -p rust/crates/degenbot-python
git mv rust/src rust/crates/degenbot-python/src
git status --short rust/   # confirm the move tracked; no content changes
```

No `.rs` file contents change in this step. Resist the urge to also touch imports â path deps inside the *cores* don't reference the binding layer, and the binding layer references cores via `degenbot_<crate>::` (external crate names, unaffected by the binding layer's own location).

### Step 2 â Write `rust/crates/degenbot-python/Cargo.toml`

Copy the `[package]`, `[lib]`, `[dependencies]`, `[features]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[[test]]`, and `[lints.*]` blocks verbatim out of the current `rust/Cargo.toml`. **Two rewrites only:**

1. **Path dependencies** â every `path = "crates/degenbot-X"` becomes `path = "../degenbot-X"` (relative to the new manifest's location). Affected lines (post-UKDOUR, all `optional = true` except core):
   ```toml
   degenbot-rpc      = { path = "../degenbot-rpc",      optional = true }
   degenbot-bot      = { path = "../degenbot-bot",      optional = true }
   degenbot-decoders = { path = "../degenbot-decoders", optional = true }
   degenbot-uniswap  = { path = "../degenbot-uniswap",  optional = true }
   degenbot-abi      = { path = "../degenbot-abi",      optional = true }
   degenbot-cl-math  = { path = "../degenbot-cl-math",  optional = true }
   degenbot-core     = { path = "../degenbot-core", features = ["pyo3"] }
   ```
2. **Dev-dependency** `degenbot-rpc` (the `test-utils` feature line) â same `../` rewrite:
   ```toml
   degenbot-rpc = { path = "../degenbot-rpc", features = ["test-utils"] }
   ```

Everything else in those blocks is byte-for-byte identical (the `[features]` table with `default = ["auto-initialize","bot","rpc","abi","cl-math","uniswap","async"]` and the `bot = ["dep:degenbot-bot","rpc","decoders","uniswap"]` implications, the `[[test]]` `required-features` entries, the `[lints.rust]`/`[lints.clippy]` deny config, the `[lib] name = "degenbot_rs" crate-type = ["rlib","cdylib"]`).

### Step 3 â Rewrite `rust/Cargo.toml` into a pure virtual manifest

Keep in `rust/Cargo.toml`:
- `[workspace]` with `resolver = "2"` â **add `crates/degenbot-python` to `members`** (alphabetical or appended; match the existing ordering style).
- The big comment block about the workspace shape (update the prose: the root is now a pure virtual manifest; `degenbot-python` is the binding layer listed as a peer of the cores).
- **`[profile.release]` + `[profile.release.package.*]` + `[profile.dev]` MUST stay here.** Cargo only honors `[profile]` in the workspace-root manifest; moving them into `crates/degenbot-python/Cargo.toml` silently breaks thin-LTO + the per-core codegen-unit overrides. This is the task's #1 gotcha. (Consider lifting `[lints.*]` to `[workspace.lints]` and having `degenbot-python` opt in via `[lints] workspace = true` â optional polish, not required for green.)

Remove from `rust/Cargo.toml` (they moved to the new package manifest in Step 2):
- `[package]`, `[lib]`, `[dependencies]`, `[features]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[[test]]`.

### Step 4 â Update `pyproject.toml` (maturin + sdist includes)

```toml
# line ~217-218 (the [tool.maturin] sdist include globs):
{file = "rust/Cargo.toml"},                                  # unchanged â virtual manifest still here
{file = "rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/**/*.rs"},          # was: rust/src/**/*.rs

# line ~222:
[tool.maturin]
manifest-path = "rust/crates/degenbot-python/Cargo.toml"     # was: rust/Cargo.toml
python-source = "src"                                        # unchanged
module-name   = "degenbot.degenbot_rs"                       # UNCHANGED â lib name preserved
```

### Step 5 â Update `justfile` (audit each `--manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml`)

Most justfile commands point at the *workspace* manifest and stay valid unchanged because `rust/Cargo.toml` still exists (now as the virtual manifest): `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace`, `cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all`, `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features`, `cargo tree --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p <crate>`, `cargo doc --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml`. **Audit and fix only these:**

- `build-rust-debug` / `build-rust-extension` / the release-build commands (lines ~44, 48, 167): `cargo build --release --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml` builds *all* workspace members under a virtual manifest; pin to `-p degenbot_rs` so a release build still produces just the cdylib: `cargo build --release -p degenbot_rs --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml` (and keep `--features extension-module` on the extension build).
- `check-no-pyo3-in-cores` (lines ~31â42): the `for crate in degenbot-core ... degenbot-uniswap` loop is unchanged (those are the pyo3-free cores). **Optional positive check** to add: `cargo tree --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p degenbot_rs | grep -qi 'pyo3 v' || { echo "ERROR: degenbot_rs must pull pyo3"; exit 1; }` â confirms the binding crate *does* have pyo3 (sanity that the split didn't invert the invariant). Not required for green; nice.

### Step 6 â Build + run every gate

```bash
just test-rust                 # workspace tests
just test-rust-python          # 211 Python tests reaching the extension
just lint-rust                 # clippy --fix --deny warnings
just check-no-pyo3-in-cores    # cores still pyo3-free (degenbot_rs is allowed pyo3)
uv run python -c "from degenbot.degenbot_rs import PyBot, UniswapArbEngine, PyLiquidityPool, PyErc20Token, decode, encode, to_checksum_address, get_sqrt_ratio_at_tick, VerificationMismatchError; print('surface ok')"
# NOTE: bare 'import degenbot_rs' has NEVER worked (maturin module-name is 'degenbot.degenbot_rs'); don't use that as a gate.
# Minimal-feature combos still build (the UKDOUR features survive the move):
cd rust && LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(python3 -c 'import sysconfig;print(sysconfig.get_config_var("LIBDIR"))')" \
  cargo build -p degenbot_rs --no-default-features --features bot   # succeeds
cd rust && cargo build -p degenbot_rs --no-default-features         # fails cleanly at build (gated symbols)
```

### Step 7 â Update LIVE docs (do NOT touch historical refs)

Update only docs describing *current* structure:
- `rust/AGENTS.md` â "#### `degenbot_rs` cdylib (binding layer)" header (line ~47): `rust/src/` â `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/`. The Layer-2 path example (line ~14) `rust/src/<domain>/<name>.rs` â `rust/crates/degenbot-python/src/<domain>/<name>.rs`. The "Module Naming Convention" prose referencing `rust/src/...`. (The per-file inventory table contents are unchanged â only the `rust/src/` path prefix in headers/prose.)
- `rust/CONTEXT.md` â any file-path refs using `rust/src/...` for binding-layer files (the post-UG6FKN refs point at `bot/engine/verify.rs` etc.; prefix with `rust/crates/degenbot-python/` or rewrite to the crate-relative `crates/degenbot-python/src/...`).
- `CONTEXT-MAP.md` â per-module `CONTEXT.md` pointers that cite `rust/src/...` binding-layer paths.
- `docs/adr/ADR-005-...md` â mark the "Crate split" deferral (lines 249â261): the *mechanical-move* portion is now DONE by this task; the *umbrella + standalone-consumer* portions remain deferred under KWTAXJ. Update the topology table (lines ~60â61) to reflect `degenbot-python` is now a real workspace member (was "name TBD").
- `BINDING-LAYER-REORG.md` â flip Status from "proposed" to "done" (the whole 7-step migration + this deferral executed); move the "Non-goals" crate-split bullet into a "Completed" note pointing at this task's commit.

**Explicitly leave as-is** (historical, document past state): `tests/perf/PROGRESS.md`, `docs/migration-guides/*`, `plans/completed/*`, ADR body text describing past `rg` surveys. These cite `rust/src/...` as it was at time of writing â correct then, not to be retroactively rewritten.

## Gotchas (read before starting)

1. **`[profile.*]` stays in the workspace manifest.** Moving `[profile.release]` / `[profile.release.package.*]` / `[profile.dev]` into the package manifest silently no-ops them (Cargo only honors `[profile]` at the workspace root). The per-core `codegen-units = 16` overrides + the cdylib `lto = "thin"` / `strip` / `codegen-units = 1` are all load-bearing for the release build.
2. **Path-dep rewrites are relative to the *new* manifest location**, not the old one. `crates/degenbot-rpc` (from `rust/Cargo.toml`) â `../degenbot-rpc` (from `rust/crates/degenbot-python/Cargo.toml`). Easy to get backwards.
3. **Do not rename the lib/package.** Keep `[lib] name = "degenbot_rs"` and `[package] name = "degenbot_rs"`. 1. **`TickInfo.block`** — added per-tick block field (mirrors Python

   uint256 width). This was the root cause of the snapshot round-trip bitmap
   mismatch (the prior session's "blocker 2 sparse-map" was partly this overflow
   masquerading as a design issue).

### Companion design decisions
- **`_bitmap_override`** — verbatim `tick_bitmap` words the builder/snapshot/
  fetcher passed via `update_tick_data`, overlaid on the Rust-derived bitmap.
  This preserves a snapshot's on-chain bitmap verbatim AND records a
  fetcher-checked empty word as present-but-zero (breaking the sparse-map
  re-fetch loop that Rust's derived-from-tick-data-keys bitmap causes).
- **`_sparse_liquidity_map`** set at construction and NOT flipped in
  `update_tick_data` — the fetcher's incremental word backfill must keep the
  pool sparse so subsequent swaps re-enter the fetch retry loop (flipping it
  made the exact-output hypothesis swap fall back to `gen_ticks` on an
  incomplete map → 36% liquidity shortfall; fixed).
- **`restore_state_before_block`** — the Rust V3 journal returns
  `result.block = oldest_popped_block` (the target convention), unlike V2's
  `landed_block`. The 3 `_state_cache` tests compare scalars (sqrt_price/
  liquidity/tick) rather than full state (which would mismatch on block).

  pre-companion had it but no caller exercised it).

## Slice 14m — DONE (committed bd54a8b2, 2026-06-21)

**Scope:** Move the hardest Balancer decode — `getPoolTokens(bytes32)` returns a tuple of shape `(address[], uint256[], uint256)` with TWO nested dynamic arrays.

### What landed

- **`PyBotIo.fetch_balancer_vault_tokens(vault_address, pool_id, block=None) -> (list[str], list[int])`** — `_fetch_vault_tokens` moves into Rust.

### Implementation note: manual decoding, not alloy DynSolType

I first attempted to use `alloy::dyn_abi::DynSolType::parse("(address[],uint256[],uint256)").abi_decode(bytes)` but it failed with `"buffer overrun while deserializing"` even on a well-formed 288-byte eth_abi-encoded tuple. So the method decodes manually:

1. Read offset to address[] data from word 0 (typically 0x60=96).
2. Read offset to uint256[] data from word 1 (typically 0xC0=192).
3. Skip the static uint256 (last block number) in word 2.
4. At each offset: read length (1 word), then walk N 32-byte element words using index arithmetic.

This reuses the `read_u256_as_usize` helper from 14l.
